title.zh: 卷78 孫紹 張普惠
title.raw: 卷78 孫紹 張普惠 Volume 78: Sun Shao, Zhang Puhui

sentences.zh: 孫紹 張普惠

translations.literal: Sun Shao; Zhang Puhui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao and Zhang Puhui.

sentences.zh: 孫紹，字世慶，昌黎人。

translations.literal: Sun Shao, styled Shiqing, was a man of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao, courtesy name Shiqing, was a native of Changli.

sentences.zh: 世仕慕容氏。

translations.literal: For generations they served the Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served the Murong for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖志入國，卒於濟陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi entered the state and died as Administrator of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi entered Wei territory and died while serving as Administrator of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 父協，字文和，上黨太守。

translations.literal: His father Xie, styled Wenhe, was Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie, courtesy name Wenhe, held the post of Administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 紹少好學，通涉經史，頗有文才，陰陽術數，多所貫涉。

translations.literal: Shao from youth loved learning, was broadly versed in the classics and histories, had considerable literary talent, and was extensively versed in yin-yang and numerological arts.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shao loved study. He ranged widely through the classics and histories, showed real literary talent, and was thoroughly versed in yin-yang lore and numerological arts.

sentences.zh: 初為校書郎，稍遷給事中，自長兼羽林監為門下錄事。

translations.literal: At first he was Proofreader, was gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and from Chief of the Feathered Forest Guard concurrently served as Recorder of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Proofreader, was gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and rose from Chief of the Feathered Forest Guard to serve concurrently as Recorder of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大事，好言得失，遂為世知。

translations.literal: On great affairs of the court he was fond of speaking of gains and losses, and thereby became known to the world.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty matters of state he was fond of speaking frankly of what worked and what failed, and in this way he came to be widely known.

sentences.zh: 曾著釋典論，雖不具美，時有可存。

translations.literal: He once wrote Discussion on Explaining the Canon; though not fully polished, parts of it are worth preserving.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a Discussion on Explaining the Canon. Though not a finished masterpiece, parts of it are still worth preserving.

sentences.zh: 與常景等共修律令。

translations.literal: Together with Chang Jing and others he jointly revised the laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Chang Jing and others he helped revise the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，紹表曰：

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era Shao submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanchang period Shao submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞建國有計，雖危必安；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in founding a state there is a plan such that even in peril one may be secure;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a state is founded with a sound plan, it can remain secure even in peril;

sentences.zh: 施化能和，雖寡必盛；

translations.literal: when transforming influence is applied harmoniously, even when few one must flourish greatly;
translations.idiomatic: when transforming influence is applied harmoniously, even a small realm can grow mighty;

sentences.zh: 治乖人理，雖合必離；

translations.literal: when government runs counter to human reason, even when united one must split apart;
translations.idiomatic: when government runs counter to human reason, even a united realm must fall apart;

sentences.zh: 作用失機，雖成必敗。

translations.literal: when action misses the opportune moment, even when accomplished one must fail.
translations.idiomatic: when action misses its moment, even what seems accomplished is doomed to fail.

sentences.zh: 此乃古今同然，百王之定法也。

translations.literal: This is the same through antiquity and the present, the fixed law of a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: This has been true in every age, the constant law of a hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大魏應天明命，兆啟無窮，畢世後仁，祚隆七百。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Great Wei responded to Heaven's bright mandate, its omens opening without end, its benevolence extending through the ages, its fortune towering for seven hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Great Wei answered Heaven's bright mandate, its auspicious signs opening without end, its benevolence extending through the ages, its fortune destined to tower for seven hundred years.

sentences.zh: 今二虢京門，下無嚴防；

translations.literal: Now at the twin Guo and the capital gates, below there is no strict defense;
translations.idiomatic: Yet today at the twin Guo and the capital gates there is no strict defense below;

sentences.zh: 南、北二中，復闕固守。

translations.literal: at the southern and northern secondary capitals again solid defense is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: and at the southern and northern secondary capitals solid garrisons are again lacking.

sentences.zh: 長安、鄴城，股肱之寄；

translations.literal: Chang'an and Ye city are the trust placed in the arms and legs;
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an and Ye are the limbs on which the realm relies;

sentences.zh: 穰城、上黨，腹背所憑。

translations.literal: Rangcheng and Shangdang are what the belly and back rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Rangcheng and Shangdang are what the belly and back depend upon.

sentences.zh: 四軍五校之軌，領、護分事之式，徵兵儲粟之要，舟車水陸之資，山河要害之權，緩急去來之用，持平赴救之方，節用應時之法，特宜修置，以固堂堂之基。

translations.literal: The tracks of the four armies and five commanderies, the forms of division of duties between commandants and protectors, the essentials of levying troops and storing grain, the resources of boats, carts, water and land, the authority over strategic passes of mountains and rivers, the use of going and coming in urgency or ease, the methods of leveling and rushing to rescue, the laws of economizing and responding to the times — all specially ought to be established and arranged to consolidate the imposing foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The organization of the four armies and five commanderies, the division of duties between commandants and protectors, the essentials of levying troops and storing grain, the resources of river and road transport, control of strategic mountain passes, provisions for urgent dispatch and relief, methods of balanced response and timely economy — all these ought specially to be put in order to consolidate our imposing foundation.

sentences.zh: 持盈之體，何得而忽？

translations.literal: The body that holds fullness — how can it be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: How can the state that holds its fullness be neglected?

sentences.zh: 居安之辰，故應危懼矣。

translations.literal: In the time of dwelling in peace, therefore one ought to fear danger.
translations.idiomatic: Precisely because we dwell in peace, we ought to fear danger.

sentences.zh: 且法開清濁，而清濁不平；

translations.literal: Moreover the law distinguishes pure from base, yet pure and base are not leveled;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the law distinguishes pure from base ranks, pure and base are not treated equally;

sentences.zh: 申滯理望，而卑寒亦免。

translations.literal: it extends to the stagnant and regulates expectations, yet the lowly and cold are also exempted.
translations.idiomatic: though it is meant to relieve stagnation and regulate expectations, the lowly and poor are also exempted.

sentences.zh: 士庶同悲，兵徒懷怨。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners alike grieve; soldiers and conscripts harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners alike grieve, while soldiers and conscripts harbor resentment.

sentences.zh: 中正賣望於下里，主按舞筆於上臺，真偽混淆，知而不糾，得者不欣，失者倍怨。

translations.literal: Rectifiers sell reputation in the villages, chief clerks flourish their brushes at the high desk, true and false are confused, those who know do not correct, those who gain are not glad, those who lose are doubly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Rectifiers sell favors in the villages while chief clerks manipulate the brush at the high desk. True and false are confused; those who know do not correct the abuse. The favored feel no joy, while the passed over are doubly resentful.

sentences.zh: 使門齊身等，而涇渭奄殊；

translations.literal: Families of equal standing and equal persons, yet Jing and Wei are utterly different;
translations.idiomatic: Families of equal standing are treated as if Jing and Wei were utterly different;

sentences.zh: 類應同役，而苦樂懸異。

translations.literal: categories that ought to share the same service, yet suffering and ease are vastly different.
translations.idiomatic: men who by category ought to share the same service find suffering and ease vastly unequal.

sentences.zh: 士人居職，不以為榮；

translations.literal: Gentry men hold office and do not regard it as honor;
translations.idiomatic: Gentry who hold office no longer regard it as an honor;

sentences.zh: 兵士役苦，心不忘亂。

translations.literal: soldiers suffer in service and in their hearts do not forget disorder.
translations.idiomatic: while soldiers, crushed by harsh service, cannot forget rebellion in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 故有競棄本出，飄藏他土。

translations.literal: Therefore some compete to abandon their roots and go out, drifting to hide in other lands.
translations.idiomatic: Hence some compete to abandon their native place and flee, drifting to hide in other regions.

sentences.zh: 或詭名託養，散在人間；

translations.literal: Some use false names and entrust themselves for support, scattered among the people;
translations.idiomatic: Some use false names and live under others' protection, scattered among the people;

sentences.zh: 或亡命山藪，漁獵為命；

translations.literal: some flee their lives into mountains and marshes, making a living by fishing and hunting;
translations.idiomatic: some flee into mountains and marshes and live by fishing and hunting;

sentences.zh: 或投仗強豪，寄命衣食。

translations.literal: some cast aside their weapons and throw themselves on powerful families, entrusting their lives for food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: some cast aside their arms and throw themselves on powerful families, staking their lives for food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 又應遷之戶，逐樂諸州；

translations.literal: Again, households that ought to be relocated pursue pleasure in various provinces;
translations.idiomatic: Again, households that ought to be relocated seek ease in other provinces;

sentences.zh: 應留之徒，避寒歸暖。

translations.literal: those who ought to remain flee the cold and return to warmth.
translations.idiomatic: while those who ought to remain flee the cold and return to warmer lands.

sentences.zh: 兼職人子弟，隨逐浮遊，南北東西，卜居莫定。

translations.literal: Sons and younger brothers of concurrent officeholders drift and wander in pursuit, north, south, east, and west, with no settled place of residence.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of men holding concurrent posts drift wherever they please, roaming north, south, east, and west with no settled home.

sentences.zh: 關禁不修，任意取適。

translations.literal: Passes and prohibitions are not maintained; they go wherever they please.
translations.idiomatic: Because passes and prohibitions are not enforced, they go wherever they please.

sentences.zh: 如此之徒，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Such persons are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Such people are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 爪牙不復為用，百工爭棄其業。

translations.literal: Claws and teeth are no longer employed; the hundred crafts compete to abandon their trades.
translations.idiomatic: The state's claws and teeth are no longer put to use, while the hundred crafts compete to abandon their trades.

sentences.zh: 混一之計，事實闕如；

translations.literal: The plan for unification in fact is lacking;
translations.idiomatic: The plan for unification is in fact nowhere to be found;

sentences.zh: 考課之方，責辦無日。

translations.literal: the method of examination and assessment has no day for fulfillment of responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: and the method of examination and assessment has no day when responsibility can actually be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 流浪之徒，決須精校。

translations.literal: Wandering persons must decisively be thoroughly checked.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering persons must be rigorously registered and checked.

sentences.zh: 今強敵窺時，邊黎伺隙，內民不平，久戍懷怨，戰國之勢，竊謂危矣。

translations.literal: Now strong enemies watch the times, frontier peoples watch for openings, the inner populace is not at peace, long garrison troops harbor resentment — the situation of warring states; I venture to say it is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Now strong enemies watch for their moment, frontier peoples watch for openings, the inner populace is unsettled, and long-garrisoned troops harbor resentment. The situation resembles that of the Warring States; I venture to say it is perilous.

sentences.zh: 必造禍源者，北邊鎮戍之人也。

translations.literal: Those who will surely create the source of disaster are the men of the northern frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Those who will surely create the source of disaster are the men of the northern frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 若夫一統之年，持平用之者，大道之計也；

translations.literal: As for the years of unified rule, using leveling and balance is the plan of the great Way;
translations.idiomatic: In years of unified rule, to employ balanced and equitable measures is the plan of the great Way;

sentences.zh: 亂離之期，縱橫作之者，行權之勢也。

translations.literal: in periods of disorder and separation, those who act with vertical and horizontal alliances follow the momentum of exercising expedient power.
translations.idiomatic: in periods of disorder and separation, to act through shifting alliances is the momentum of exercising expedient power.

sentences.zh: 故道不可久，須文質以換情；

translations.literal: Therefore the Way cannot long endure; one must use culture and substance to exchange sentiments;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Way cannot long endure unchanged; culture and substance must alternate to meet the people's needs;

sentences.zh: 權不可恒，隨洿隆以收物。

translations.literal: expedient power cannot be constant; one follows the low and high to gather things.
translations.idiomatic: nor can expedient power remain constant; one must follow rise and decline to gather the realm.

sentences.zh: 文質應世，道形自安；

translations.literal: When culture and substance respond to the age, the form of the Way is naturally secure;
translations.idiomatic: When culture and substance respond to the age, the Way takes secure form;

sentences.zh: 洿隆獲衷，權勢亦濟。

translations.literal: when low and high obtain the mean, expedient power also succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: when rise and decline obtain the mean, expedient power also succeeds.

sentences.zh: 然則，王者計法之趣，化物之規，圓方務得其境，人物不失其地。

translations.literal: Thus the aim of the king's method of planning, the rule for transforming things, is that round and square each obtain their proper sphere and persons and things do not lose their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the aim of a king's planning and the rule for transforming the realm is that round and square each find their proper sphere, and persons and things do not lose their proper place.

sentences.zh: 又先帝時，律令並議，律尋施行，令獨不出，十餘年矣。

translations.literal: Again, in the time of the late emperor, statutes and ordinances were jointly deliberated; the statutes were soon put into effect, but the ordinances alone were not issued — more than ten years now.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in the late emperor's time statutes and ordinances were jointly deliberated. The statutes were soon put into effect, but the ordinances alone have not been issued — for more than ten years now.

sentences.zh: 臣以令之為體，即帝王之身也，分處百揆之儀，安置九服之節，經緯三才之倫，包羅六卿之職，措置風化之門，作用賞罰之要，乃是有為之樞機，世法之大本也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the substance of ordinances is none other than the body of the emperor: the rites for apportioning the hundred duties, the regulations for arranging the nine domains, the warp and woof of the three powers' order, embracing the duties of the six ministers, setting up the gate of transforming influence, applying the essentials of reward and punishment — these are the pivot of positive action and the great foundation of the law of the age.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that ordinances are the very body of the emperor: they apportion the rites of the hundred duties, arrange the regulations of the nine domains, weave the order of the three powers, embrace the duties of the six ministers, set up the gate of transforming influence, and apply the essentials of reward and punishment. They are the pivot of active governance and the great foundation of the law of the age.

sentences.zh: 然修令之人，亦皆博古，依古撰置，大體可觀，比之前令，精粗有在。

translations.literal: Yet those who revised the ordinances were all broadly versed in antiquity; following antiquity they composed and arranged them — the general outline is worth viewing; compared with previous ordinances, there is substance in both refinement and roughness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who revised the ordinances were all broadly learned in antiquity. Following ancient models they composed them, and the general outline is sound. Compared with earlier ordinances, there is real substance in both refinement and roughness.

sentences.zh: 但主議之家，太用古制。

translations.literal: But the families leading the deliberation relied too heavily on ancient institutions.
translations.idiomatic: But the families leading the deliberation relied too heavily on ancient institutions.

sentences.zh: 若全依古，高祖之法，復須昇降，誰敢措意有是非哉？

translations.literal: If one wholly followed antiquity, even the laws of High Emperor would again need raising and lowering — who would dare set forth an opinion of right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: If one followed antiquity entirely, even the laws of Emperor Gaozu would again need raising and lowering. Who would dare express an opinion on what was right or wrong?

sentences.zh: 以是爭故，久廢不理。

translations.literal: Because of these disputes, they were long abandoned and not brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: Because of these disputes they have long lain abandoned and unratified.

sentences.zh: 然律令相須，不可偏用，今律班令止，於事甚滯。

translations.literal: Yet statutes and ordinances depend on each other and cannot be used one-sidedly; now the statutes are promulgated while the ordinances are halted — affairs are greatly impeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet statutes and ordinances depend on each other and cannot be used alone. Now the statutes are promulgated while the ordinances are halted, and affairs are greatly impeded.

sentences.zh: 若令不班，是無典法，臣下執事，何依而行？

translations.literal: If the ordinances are not promulgated, there is no canonical law — on what basis do subordinates in office act?
translations.idiomatic: If the ordinances are not promulgated, there is no canonical law. On what basis are subordinates in office to act?

sentences.zh: 臣等修律，非無勤止，署下之日，臣乃無名。

translations.literal: Your servants and others in revising the statutes were not without diligence and effort, yet on the day of signing and issuing them your servant had no name.
translations.idiomatic: We who revised the statutes were not without diligence, yet on the day they were signed and issued my name was nowhere to be found.

sentences.zh: 是謂農夫盡力，他食其秋，功名之所，實懷於悒。

translations.literal: This is to say the farmer exhausts his strength while another eats his autumn harvest; as to where merit and fame lie, I truly harbor distress.
translations.idiomatic: It is as though the farmer exhausts his strength while another eats his autumn harvest. As to where merit and fame lie, I truly harbor distress.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出除濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out and appointed Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out and appointed Administrator of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 還，歷司徒功曹參軍，步兵、長水校尉。

translations.literal: On return he successively served as Registrar in the Merit Section of the Minister of Education, and as Commandant of the Footsoldiers and Commandant of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served successively as Registrar in the Merit Section of the Minister of Education and as Commandant of the Footsoldiers and Commandant of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 正光初，兼中書侍郎，使高麗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang he concurrently served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was sent as envoy to Koguryŏ.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengguang era he concurrently served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was sent as envoy to Koguryŏ.

sentences.zh: 還，為鎮遠將軍、右軍將軍。

translations.literal: On return he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 久之，為徐兗和糴使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made Commissioner for Harmonious Grain Purchase in Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Commissioner for Harmonious Grain Purchase in Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 還朝，大陳軍國利害，不報。

translations.literal: On return to court he set forth at length the advantages and harms to army and state, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to court he set forth at length the advantages and harms to army and state, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 紹又表曰：「臣聞文質互用，治道以之緝熙；

translations.literal: Shao again submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that culture and substance are used in alternation, and by this the way of governance is brought to brightness;
translations.idiomatic: Shao again submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that culture and substance are used in alternation, and by this the way of governance is brought to brightness;

sentences.zh: 洿隆得時，人物以之通濟。

translations.literal: when low and high obtain their season, persons and things thereby pass through smoothly.
translations.idiomatic: when rise and decline obtain their proper season, persons and things thereby pass through smoothly.

sentences.zh: 故能事恢三靈，仁洽九服。

translations.literal: Thus affairs can extend to the three numina and benevolence can pervade the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: Thus affairs can extend to the three numina and benevolence can pervade the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下應靈踐阼，沖明照物，宰輔忠純，伊霍均美，既致昇平之基，應成無為之業。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty responded to the numina and ascended the throne, with pure clarity illuminating things; the chief ministers are loyal and pure, equal in beauty to Yi Yin and Huo Guang; you have already brought about the foundation of rising peace and ought to complete the enterprise of non-action.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty answered the numina and ascended the throne, your pure clarity illuminating all things. Your chief ministers are loyal and upright, equal in renown to Yi Yin and Huo Guang. You have already laid the foundation of rising peace and ought to complete the enterprise of effortless rule.

sentences.zh: 而漠北叛命，隴右構逆，中州驚擾，民庶竊議，其故何哉？

translations.literal: Yet the desert north rebels against orders, Longyou constructs treason, the central provinces are alarmed and disturbed, and the people whisper in private discussion — what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the desert north rebels, Longyou raises treason, the central provinces are alarmed, and the people whisper in private — what is the reason?

sentences.zh: 皆由上法不通，下情怨塞故也。

translations.literal: All are because the law above does not penetrate and resentment below is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: It is all because the law above does not penetrate and resentment below is blocked.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚短，具鑒始末。

translations.literal: Your servant, though foolish and short-sighted, fully perceives the beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am foolish and short-sighted, I see the beginning and end clearly.

sentences.zh: 往在代都，武質而治安；

translations.literal: Formerly at the capital in Dai, martial substance brought peace and order;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly at the capital in Dai, martial substance brought peace and order;

sentences.zh: 中京以來，文華而政亂。

translations.literal: since the central capital, literary splendor but governmental disorder.
translations.idiomatic: since the move to the central capital, literary splendor but governmental disorder.

sentences.zh: 故臣昔於太和，極陳得失，具論四方華夷心態，高祖垂納，文應可尋。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant formerly in the Taihe era set forth gains and losses to the utmost, fully discussed the attitudes of Chinese and barbarian in the four directions; High Emperor leaned down and accepted it, and the text can still be traced.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I formerly in the Taihe era set forth gains and losses to the utmost and fully discussed the attitudes of Chinese and barbarian across the four directions. Emperor Gaozu accepted it, and the text can still be traced.

sentences.zh: 延昌、正光，奏疏頻上，主者收錄，不蒙報問，即日事勢，乃至於此，盡微臣豫陳之驗。

translations.literal: In Yanchang and Zhengguang memorials were frequently submitted; the responsible offices received and recorded them but received no response or inquiry. The situation of the day has reached this point — all verification of what your humble servant foretold.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang and Zhengguang memorials were frequently submitted. The responsible offices received and recorded them but gave no response. The situation of the day has reached this point — all verification of what I foretold.

sentences.zh: 今東南有竊號之豎，西北有逆命之寇，豈得怨天，實尤人矣。

translations.literal: Now in the southeast there is a petty fellow who has stolen a title, in the northwest there are bandits who oppose orders — how can one blame Heaven? In truth the blame lies with men.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the southeast there is a petty man who has stolen a title, and in the northwest there are bandits who oppose our orders. How can one blame Heaven? In truth the blame lies with men.

sentences.zh: 臣今不憂荒外，正慮中畿，急須改張，以寧其意。

translations.literal: Your servant now does not worry about the wild outer regions but rightly worries about the central domains; reform must urgently be carried out to settle their minds.
translations.idiomatic: I do not now worry about the wild outer regions but rightly worry about the central domains. Reform must urgently be carried out to settle the people's minds.

sentences.zh: 若仍持疑，變亂尋作，肘腋一乖，大事去矣。

translations.literal: If one still holds to doubt, change and disorder will soon arise; once the armpit and flank are at odds, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If you still hold to doubt, change and disorder will soon arise. Once those at your very side turn against you, the great affair is lost.

sentences.zh: 然臣奉國四世，欣戚是同，但職在冗散，不關樞密，寧濟之計，欲陳無所，可謂經緯甚多，無機可織。

translations.literal: Yet your servant has served the state for four generations and shares the same joy and sorrow; only my post is among the redundant and scattered, not connected with vital secrets — plans to bring peace have nowhere to be set forth. One may say there is much to weave but no loom on which to weave.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have served the state for four generations and share its joy and sorrow. Only my post is among the redundant and scattered, with no access to vital secrets. Plans to bring peace have nowhere to be set forth. One may say there is much to weave but no loom on which to weave.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，大器也。

translations.literal: The realm under Heaven is a great vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The realm under Heaven is a great vessel.

sentences.zh: 一正難傾，一傾難正。

translations.literal: Once upright it is hard to overturn; once overturned it is hard to set upright.
translations.idiomatic: Once upright it is hard to overturn; once overturned it is hard to set upright.

sentences.zh: 當今之危，躡足之急，臣備肉食，痛心無已。

translations.literal: The peril of the present is the urgency of treading on one's foot; your servant, though provisioned with meat, is endlessly pained at heart.
translations.idiomatic: The peril of the present is the urgency of a misstep. Though I am provisioned with meat at court, my heart is endlessly pained.

sentences.zh: 泣血上陳，願垂採察。

translations.literal: Weeping blood I submit this above; I beg that you lean down and examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping blood I submit this above and beg that you examine it.

sentences.zh: 若得言參執事，獻可替否，寇逆獲除，社稷稱慶，雖死如生，犬馬情畢。」

translations.literal: If I may have my words join those who hold office, offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not, and the bandits and rebels are removed and the altars of soil and grain rejoice, though dead it would be as living — my feeling as hound and horse would be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: If I may join those who hold office, offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not, and the bandits and rebels are removed so that the altars of soil and grain rejoice, though dead it would be as living and my devotion as hound and horse would be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 紹性抗直，每上封事，常至懇切，不憚犯忤。

translations.literal: Shao's nature was upright and direct; each time he submitted a sealed memorial it was often to the point of earnestness, not fearing to give offense.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's nature was upright and direct. Each time he submitted a sealed memorial he spoke with earnest force and did not fear giving offense.

sentences.zh: 但天性疏脫，言乍高下，時人輕之，不見採納。

translations.literal: But by nature he was loose and unguarded; his words suddenly rose and fell, and men of the time slighted him and did not adopt his views.
translations.idiomatic: But by nature he was loose and unguarded, his words suddenly rising and falling. Men of the time slighted him and did not adopt his views.

sentences.zh: 紹兄世元早卒，世元善彈箏，紹後聞箏聲便涕泗嗚咽，捨之而去，世以此尚之。

translations.literal: Shao's elder brother Shiyuan died early. Shiyuan was skilled at playing the zither; afterward when Shao heard the sound of the zither he would weep and sob, set it aside and leave — the world for this held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's elder brother Shiyuan died early. Shiyuan had been skilled at playing the zither. Later, when Shao heard the zither played he would weep and sob, then set it aside and leave. The world for this held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 除驍騎將軍，使吐谷渾。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and sent as envoy to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and sent as envoy to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 還，為太府少卿。

translations.literal: On return he was made Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 曾因朝見，靈太后謂曰：「卿年稍老矣。」

translations.literal: Once during an audience at court, Empress Dowager Ling said to him: "Your age is somewhat advanced."
translations.idiomatic: Once during an audience at court, Empress Dowager Ling said to him, "You are getting somewhat old."

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「臣年雖老，臣卿乃少。」

translations.literal: Shao said: "Though your servant's years are old, your servant's 'qing' is still young."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Though my years are old, my qing is still young."

sentences.zh: 太后笑之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager laughed at this.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager laughed at this.

sentences.zh: 遷右將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 紹曾與百僚赴朝，東掖未開，守門候旦。

translations.literal: Shao once went to court with the hundred officials; the eastern side gate was not yet open, and he waited at the gate for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Shao once went to court with the hundred officials. The eastern side gate was not yet open, and he waited at the gate for dawn.

sentences.zh: 紹於眾中引吏部郎中辛雄於眾外，竊謂之曰：「此中諸人，尋當死盡，唯吾與卿猶享富貴。」

translations.literal: Shao, from among the crowd, led Xin Xiong, Master of the Palace in the Ministry of Personnel, outside the crowd and whispered to him, saying: "All the people here will soon die to the last man; only you and I will still enjoy wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Among the waiting officials, Shao drew Xin Xiong, Master of the Palace in the Ministry of Personnel, aside from the crowd and whispered to him: "Everyone here will soon be dead to the last man. Only you and I will still enjoy wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 雄甚駭愕，不測所以。

translations.literal: Xin was greatly appalled and could not fathom the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was deeply shaken and could not guess what Shao meant.

sentences.zh: 未幾有河陰之難。

translations.literal: Before long there was the catastrophe at River Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came the massacre at River Yin.

sentences.zh: 紹善推祿命，事驗甚多，知者異之。

translations.literal: Shao was skilled at calculating fate from salary and destiny; many matters proved true, and those who knew of it were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was skilled at reading fate from salary and destiny, and many of his predictions came true. Those who knew of it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除衞尉少卿，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court for the Palace Guard, his generalship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court for the Palace Guard, retaining his generalship as before.

sentences.zh: 轉金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Tassel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Tassel.

sentences.zh: 永安中，拜太府卿。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 以前參議正光壬子曆，賜爵新昌子。

translations.literal: For having previously participated in deliberating on the Zhenguang renszi calendar, he was granted the title Marquis of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: For his earlier participation in deliberating on the Zhenguang renszi calendar, he was granted the title Marquis of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，遷左衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taichang era, he was transferred to General of the Left Guard and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era, he was transferred to General of the Left Guard and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yongxi, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈都督冀瀛滄三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、冀州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Commander-in-Chief over all military affairs of the three provinces of Ji, Ying, and Cang, General-in-Chief of Fast Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Ji Province; his posthumous name was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted command over all military affairs of Ji, Ying, and Cang provinces, the title General-in-Chief of Fast Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Ji Province. His posthumous name was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子伯元，襲。

translations.literal: His son Boyuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boyuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 伯元弟叔利，右將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Boyuan's younger brother Shuli was General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan's younger brother Shuli served as General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 紹從父弟瑜，濟州長史。

translations.literal: Shao's father's younger cousin's son Yu was Chief Clerk of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's father's younger cousin's son Yu served as Chief Clerk of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 瑜弟彝，字鳳倫。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Yi, styled Fenglun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Yi, courtesy name Fenglun.

sentences.zh: 太和中，舉秀才。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era, he was recommended as a Cultivated Talent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era, he was recommended as a Cultivated Talent.

sentences.zh: 稍遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 卒於武邑太守。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Administrator of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Administrator of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、營州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the title General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 子伯融，出繼瑜後。

translations.literal: His son Borong was given in adoption to continue Yu's line.
translations.idiomatic: His son Borong was given in adoption to continue Yu's line.

sentences.zh: 武定末，□□太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, [title missing] Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era, he served as [title missing] Administrator.

sentences.zh: 伯融嫡弟子寬，開府田曹參軍。

translations.literal: Borong's eldest legitimate nephew Kuan was Army Clerk of the Field Office under an Opening General.
translations.idiomatic: Borong's eldest legitimate nephew Kuan served as Army Clerk of the Field Office under an Opening General.

sentences.zh: 張普惠，字洪賑，常山九門人。

translations.literal: Zhang Puhui, styled Hongzhen, was a man of Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Puhui, courtesy name Hongzhen, was a native of Jiumen in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，容貌魁偉。

translations.literal: His body was eight feet in height, and his appearance was imposing and grand.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall, with an imposing and striking appearance.

sentences.zh: 父曄，為齊州中水縣令，隨父之縣，受業齊土，專心墳典，克厲不息。

translations.literal: His father Ye served as Magistrate of Zhongshui County in Qi Province. Following his father to the county, he received instruction in Qi territory, devoted himself to the classics, and labored at self-discipline without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ye served as Magistrate of Zhongshui County in Qi Province. Puhui followed his father to the county, studied in Qi territory, devoted himself to the classics, and disciplined himself without rest.

sentences.zh: 及還鄉里，就程玄講習，精於三禮，兼善春秋，百家之說，多所窺覽，諸儒稱之。

translations.literal: When he returned to his homeland, he studied under Cheng Xuan, became expert in the Three Rites, was also skilled in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and perused widely the teachings of the hundred schools; the Confucian scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home, he studied under Cheng Xuan. He mastered the Three Rites, was also skilled in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and read widely among the teachings of the hundred schools. The Confucian scholars praised him.

sentences.zh: 太和十九年，為主書，帶制局監，與劉桃符、石榮、劉道斌同員共直，頗為高祖所知。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taihe, he served as Master of Documents, concurrently holding the post of Supervisor of the Bureau of Regulations, and was on the same roster and duty rotation with Liu Taofu, Shi Rong, and Liu Daobin; he came to be rather well known to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Taihe, he served as Master of Documents and concurrently as Supervisor of the Bureau of Regulations. He shared roster and duty rotation with Liu Taofu, Shi Rong, and Liu Daobin, and came to be well regarded by Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書都令史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄重其學業，為其聲價，僕射李沖曾至澄處，見普惠言論，亦善之。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng valued his learning and boosted his reputation. Vice Director Li Chong once came to Cheng's residence, saw Puhui's discourse, and also approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng valued his learning and helped raise his reputation. Vice Director Li Chong once visited Cheng's residence, heard Puhui speak, and was also impressed.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，轉積射將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, he was transferred to General of Accumulated Arrows.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, he was transferred to General of Accumulated Arrows.

sentences.zh: 澄為安西將軍、雍州刺史，啟普惠為府錄事參軍，尋行馮翊郡事。

translations.literal: When Cheng became General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong Province, he recommended Puhui as Recorder of the Headquarters Staff, and soon had him administer the affairs of Fengyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng became General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong Province, he recommended Puhui as Recorder of the Headquarters Staff and soon had him administer the affairs of Fengyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 澄功衰在身，欲於七月七日集會文武，北園馬射。

translations.literal: Cheng was wearing gong-shuai mourning, yet wished on the seventh day of the seventh month to assemble civil and military officials for mounted archery in the Northern Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was still in gong-shuai mourning, yet planned on the seventh day of the seventh month to gather civil and military officials for mounted archery in the Northern Garden.

sentences.zh: 普惠奏記於澄曰：「竊聞三殺九親，別疏昵之敍；

translations.literal: Puhui submitted a memorial to Cheng, saying: "I have heard that the three kills and nine kin distinguish the order between distant and close relations;
translations.idiomatic: Puhui submitted a memorial to Cheng, saying: "I have heard that the 'three kills' and 'nine kin' distinguish the order between distant and close relations;

sentences.zh: 五服六術，等衰麻之心。

translations.literal: the five grades of mourning garments and six techniques equalize the heart in sackcloth.
translations.idiomatic: the five grades of mourning garments and six techniques equalize the heart that wears sackcloth.

sentences.zh: 皆因事飾情，不易之道者也。

translations.literal: All adapt expression to circumstance — this is the unchanging Way.
translations.idiomatic: All of these adapt outward expression to inward feeling — the unchanging Way.

sentences.zh: 然則莫大之痛，深於終身之外；

translations.literal: Thus the greatest grief extends deeper than a lifetime;
translations.idiomatic: The greatest grief, then, extends beyond a lifetime;

sentences.zh: 書策之哀，除於喪紀之內。

translations.literal: the sorrow recorded in written ordinances is discharged within the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: while the sorrow set down in written ordinances is discharged within the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 外者不可無節，故斷之以三年；

translations.literal: What is outward cannot be without measure, and so it is cut off at three years;
translations.idiomatic: What is outward cannot be without measure, and so it is cut off at three years;

sentences.zh: 內者不可遂除，故敦之以日月。

translations.literal: what is inward cannot be immediately removed, and so it is strengthened through months and days.
translations.idiomatic: what is inward cannot be immediately cast off, and so it is sustained through months and days.

sentences.zh: 禮，大練之日，鼓素琴。

translations.literal: In ritual, on the day of the da-lian, one strikes the plain zither.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say that on the day of the da-lian, one may strike the plain zither.

sentences.zh: 蓋推以即吉也。

translations.literal: This is presumably pushing toward returning to auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: That is presumably a step toward returning to auspicious living.

sentences.zh: 小功以上，非虞祔練除不沐浴，此拘之以制也。

translations.literal: For mourning of xiao-gong and above, one does not bathe except at the yu, fu, and lian removals — this is restraining by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For mourning of xiao-gong and above, one does not bathe except at the yu, fu, and lian removals. This is restraint by regulation.

sentences.zh: 曾子問曰：『相識有喪服，可以與於祭乎？』

translations.literal: Zengzi asked: "If an acquaintance is in mourning garments, may one participate in a sacrifice with him?"
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi asked: "If an acquaintance is in mourning garments, may one take part in a sacrifice with him?"

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『緦不祭，又何助於人。』

translations.literal: Confucius said: "One in si mourning does not sacrifice — how then could one assist others?"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "One in si mourning does not sacrifice. How then could one assist others?"

sentences.zh: 祭既不與，疑無宴食之道。

translations.literal: If one does not participate in sacrifice, it seems there is no way to feasting and eating.
translations.idiomatic: If one may not take part in sacrifice, it seems there should be no way to feasting and dining either.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『廢喪服，可以與於饋奠之事乎？』

translations.literal: Again he asked: "If one has discarded mourning garments, may one participate in the presentation of offerings?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: "If one has cast off mourning garments, may one take part in presenting offerings?"

sentences.zh: 子曰：『脫衰與奠，非禮也。』

translations.literal: The Master said: "Putting off reduced mourning and presenting offerings is not in accord with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The Master said: "Putting off reduced mourning and presenting offerings is not in accord with ritual."

sentences.zh: 注云：『為其忘哀疾。』

translations.literal: The commentary says: "Because one has forgotten grief too hastily."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "Because one has cast off grief too hastily."

sentences.zh: 愚謂除喪之始，不與饋奠，小功之內，其可觀射乎？

translations.literal: I venture to say that at the beginning of removing mourning one does not participate in presenting offerings — within the period of xiao-gong mourning, can one watch archery?
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that at the very start of removing mourning one does not take part in presenting offerings. Within the period of xiao-gong mourning, how can one watch archery?

sentences.zh: 雜記云：『大功以下，既葬適人，人食之，其黨也食之，非黨也不食。』

translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Records say: "Below da-gong mourning, after the burial when visiting others, if the host eats, those of his party eat; those not of his party do not eat."
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Records say: "Below da-gong mourning, after the burial when visiting others, if the host eats, those of his party may eat; those not of his party may not."

sentences.zh: 食猶擇人，於射為惑。

translations.literal: Even in eating one still selects company — in archery this would be all the more doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Even in eating one still chooses one's company. Archery would be all the more doubtful.

sentences.zh: 伏見明教，立射會之限，將以二七令辰，集城中文武，肄武藝於北園，行揖讓於中否。

translations.literal: I humbly observe Your Bright Instruction setting a limit for an archery assembly on the twenty-seventh auspicious day, gathering civil and military officials within the city to drill martial skills in the Northern Garden and perform bowing and yielding in the central court.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe Your Bright Instruction setting a date for an archery assembly on the twenty-seventh day, gathering civil and military officials within the city to drill martial skills in the Northern Garden and perform the bowing and yielding in the central court.

sentences.zh: 時非大閱之秋，景涉妨農之節，國家縞禫甫除，殿下功衰仍襲，釋而為樂，以訓百姓，便是易先王之典教，忘哀戚之情，恐非所以昭令德、視子孫者也。

translations.literal: This is not the season for the great autumn review; the season already touches on the time that hampers farming. The state has just ended its white-hemp mourning, yet Your Highness still wears gong-shuai mourning. To cast this off for pleasure in order to instruct the common people would be to alter the canonical teaching of the former kings and forget the feelings of grief and sorrow — I fear this is not the way to display fine virtue and show an example to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: This is not the season for the great autumn review, and the season already encroaches on the time that hampers farming. The state has only just ended its white-hemp mourning, yet Your Highness still wears gong-shuai mourning. To cast mourning aside for pleasure in order to instruct the common people would be to alter the canonical teaching of the former kings and forget grief and sorrow. I fear this is not the way to display fine virtue and set an example for posterity.

sentences.zh: 按射儀，射者以禮樂為本，忘而從事，不可謂禮，鍾鼓弗設，不可謂樂。

translations.literal: According to the Archery Rites, archers take ritual and music as their root. To forget these and proceed cannot be called ritual; if bells and drums are not set out, it cannot be called music.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Archery Rites, archers take ritual and music as their foundation. To forget these and proceed cannot be called ritual; if bells and drums are not set out, it cannot be called music.

sentences.zh: 捨此二者，何用射為？

translations.literal: Abandoning these two, of what use is archery?
translations.idiomatic: If these two are set aside, what is archery for?

sentences.zh: 又七日之戲，令制無之，班勞所施，慮違事體。

translations.literal: Moreover, the games of the seventh day are not in the current regulations. The distribution of rewards and recognition, I fear, would violate the substance of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the games of the seventh day are not provided for in current regulations. The distribution of rewards and honors, I fear, would violate the substance of the affair.

sentences.zh: 庫府空虛，宜待新調，二三之趣，停之為便。

translations.literal: The treasury is empty; one ought to wait for new allocations. As for this matter, it would be better to suspend it.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is empty, and one ought to wait for new allocations. As for this plan, it would be better to suspend it.

sentences.zh: 乞至九月，備飾盡行，然後奏狸首之章，宣矍相之令，聲軒懸，建雲鉦，神民忻暢於斯時也。

translations.literal: I beg that it be postponed until the ninth month, when preparations are complete, and then perform the "Li Shou" chapter, proclaim the commands of the archery master, hang the bell frame, and erect the cloud gongs — let spirits and people rejoice together at that time.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that it be postponed until the ninth month, when all preparations are complete, and then perform the "Li Shou" chapter, proclaim the commands of the archery master, hang the bell frame, and erect the cloud gongs, so that spirits and people may rejoice together at that time.

sentences.zh: 伏惟慈明遠被，萬民是望，舉動所書，發言唯則，願更廣訪，賜垂曲採，昭其管見之心，恕其讜言之責，則芻蕘無遺歌，輿人有獻誦矣。」

translations.literal: May Your Benevolent Clarity extend far; the myriad people look to you. Every act you record and every word you speak serves as a standard. I beg you to consult more widely and bestow your gracious acceptance, making manifest this narrow vision and pardoning this duty of frank counsel — then even the firewood-gatherer's song will not be left out, and the common traveler will have a verse to offer."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Benevolent Clarity extend far, for the myriad people look to you. Every act you record and every word you speak serves as a standard. I beg you to consult more widely and grant your gracious acceptance, making manifest this narrow vision and pardoning this duty of frank counsel. Then even the firewood-gatherer's song will not be left unsung, and the common traveler will have a verse to offer."

sentences.zh: 澄意納其言，託辭自罷，乃答曰：「文武之道，自昔成規；

translations.literal: Cheng was minded to accept his words and used an excuse to cancel the event himself, then replied: "The way of civil and military affairs has been a fixed rule since ancient times;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was inclined to accept his words and used an excuse to cancel the event himself. He then replied: "The way of civil and military affairs has been a fixed rule since ancient times;

sentences.zh: 明耻教戰，振古常軌。

translations.literal: to make clear the shame of warfare and teach battle has been the constant track from time immemorial.
translations.idiomatic: to make clear the shame of warfare and teach battle has been the constant path from time immemorial.

sentences.zh: 今雖非公制，而此州承前，已有斯式，既不勞民損公，任其私射，復何失也？

translations.literal: Though it is not now an official regulation, this province following precedent already has this practice. Since it neither burdens the people nor harms the public treasury, letting them shoot privately — what harm is there?
translations.idiomatic: Though it is not now an official regulation, this province, following precedent, already has this practice. Since it neither burdens the people nor harms the public treasury, letting them shoot privately — what harm is there?

sentences.zh: 且纂文習武，人之常藝，豈可於常藝之間，要須令制乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, studying literature and practicing martial arts are the ordinary skills of men — must ordinary skills always require official regulations?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, studying literature and practicing martial arts are ordinary human skills. Must ordinary skills always require official regulations?

sentences.zh: 比適欲依前州府相率，王務之暇，肄藝良辰，亦未言費用庫物也。

translations.literal: I had merely wished to follow the former practice of the provincial government gathering together, in the leisure from princely duties, to drill skills at an auspicious time — I had not even spoken of spending treasury goods.
translations.idiomatic: I had merely wished to follow the former practice of the provincial government gathering together, in the leisure from princely duties, to drill skills at an auspicious time. I had not even spoken of spending treasury goods.

sentences.zh: 禮，兄弟內除，明哀已殺；

translations.literal: In ritual, inner removal for a brother shows that grief has diminished;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say that inner removal for a brother shows that grief has already diminished;

sentences.zh: 小功，客至主不絕樂。

translations.literal: in xiao-gong mourning, when a guest arrives the host does not stop music.
translations.idiomatic: in xiao-gong mourning, when a guest arrives the host does not stop the music.

sentences.zh: 聽樂則可，觀武豈傷？

translations.literal: If hearing music is permitted, how could watching martial display be harmful?
translations.idiomatic: If hearing music is permitted, how could watching martial display do harm?

sentences.zh: 直自事緣須罷，先以令停，方獲此請，深具來意。」

translations.literal: It is simply that the matter itself required cancellation; I had already ordered it stopped, and only now receive this request — I deeply appreciate the intent behind it."
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that the matter itself required cancellation. I had already ordered it stopped, and only now receive this request. I deeply appreciate the intent behind it."

sentences.zh: 澄轉揚州，啟普惠以羽林監領鎮南大將軍開府主簿，尋加威遠將軍。

translations.literal: Cheng was transferred to Yang Province and recommended Puhui to serve concurrently as Chief of the Feathered Forest Guard while leading the Chief Clerk of the Opening Staff of the General Who Guards the South; soon he was additionally appointed General Who Displays Distant Might.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was transferred to Yang Province and recommended Puhui to serve concurrently as Chief of the Feathered Forest Guard and Chief Clerk of the Opening Staff of the General Who Guards the South. Soon he was additionally appointed General Who Displays Distant Might.

sentences.zh: 普惠既為澄所知，歷佐二藩，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: Since Puhui was valued by Cheng, he served successively at two princely establishments and gained considerable renown.
translations.idiomatic: Once Puhui had won Cheng's esteem, he served successively at two princely establishments and gained considerable renown.

sentences.zh: 旋京之日，裝束藍縷，澄賚絹二十匹以充行資。

translations.literal: On the day he returned to the capital, his clothing was in rags; Cheng bestowed twenty bolts of silk to supply his travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he returned to the capital, his clothing was in rags. Cheng bestowed twenty bolts of silk to supply his travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 還朝，仍羽林監。

translations.literal: After returning to court, he resumed his post as Chief of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court, he resumed his post as Chief of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 又澄遭太妃憂，臣僚為立碑頌，題碑欲云「康王元妃之碑。」

translations.literal: Again, when Cheng was in mourning for the Grand Consort, his officials proposed erecting a commemorative stele. They wished to inscribe it: "Stele of the Primary Consort of Prince Kang."
translations.idiomatic: Again, when Cheng was in mourning for the Grand Consort, his officials proposed erecting a commemorative stele. They wished to inscribe it: "Stele of the Primary Consort of Prince Kang."

sentences.zh: 澄訪於普惠。

translations.literal: Cheng consulted Puhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng consulted Puhui.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「謹尋朝典，但有王妃，而無元字。

translations.literal: He replied: "I have carefully examined the court regulations: there is 'royal consort' but no character yuan ('primary').
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I have carefully examined the court regulations. They provide for 'royal consort,' but not for the character yuan, 'primary.

sentences.zh: 魯夫人孟子稱『元妃』者，欲下與『繼室聲子』相對。

translations.literal: When Mencius called the Lady of Lu the 'Primary Consort,' he wished to set her below and in contrast with 'the successor consort Shengzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Mencius called the Lady of Lu the 'Primary Consort,' he wished to set her below and in contrast with 'the successor consort Shengzi.

sentences.zh: 今烈懿太妃作配先王，更無聲子、仲子之嫌，竊謂不假『元』字以別名位。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Consort Lieyi was matched to the former king, with no concern about a successor consort like Shengzi or Zhongzi; I venture to say there is no need to borrow the character yuan to distinguish rank.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Consort Lieyi was matched to the former king, with none of the complications of a successor consort such as Shengzi or Zhongzi. I venture to say there is no need to borrow the character yuan to distinguish rank.

sentences.zh: 且以氏配姓，愚以為在生之稱。

translations.literal: Moreover, pairing the clan name with the surname — I think this is a form of address for while one is alive.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, pairing the clan name with the surname — I think that is a form of address used while one is alive.

sentences.zh: 故春秋，『夫人姜氏至自齊』，既葬，以諡配姓，故經書『葬我小君文姜氏』，[2]又曰『來歸夫人成風之襚』。

translations.literal: Thus in the Spring and Autumn Annals, "The Lady Jiang arrived from Qi" — after the burial, with the posthumous name paired with the clan name, the classic records "We buried our lesser lady, Lady Wen Jiang," [2] and again says "They came back with the funeral offerings for the lady Chengfeng."
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the Spring and Autumn Annals, "The Lady Jiang arrived from Qi." After the burial, with the posthumous name paired with the clan name, the classic records "We buried our lesser lady, Lady Wen Jiang," [2] and again says "They came back with the funeral offerings for the lady Chengfeng."

sentences.zh: 皆以諡配姓。

translations.literal: In all cases the posthumous name is paired with the clan name.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases the posthumous name is paired with the clan name.

sentences.zh: 古者婦人從夫諡。

translations.literal: In antiquity women took their husbands' posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity women took their husbands' posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 今烈懿太妃德冠一世，故特蒙褒錫，乃萬代之高事，豈容於定名之重，而不稱烈懿乎？」

translations.literal: Now the Grand Consort Lieyi's virtue surpassed her age, and she was specially granted this honored epithet — a matter lofty enough to last ten thousand generations. How could one, in settling so weighty a name, fail to use Lieyi?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Consort Lieyi's virtue surpassed her age, and she was specially granted this honored epithet — a matter lofty enough to last ten thousand generations. How could one, in settling so weighty a name, fail to use Lieyi?"

sentences.zh: 澄從之。

translations.literal: Cheng followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 及王師大舉，重征鍾離，普惠為安樂王詮別將長史。

translations.literal: When the royal army launched its great campaign and again marched against Zhongli, Puhui served as Chief Clerk to the Separate Commander under Prince Anle, Yuan Quan.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal army launched its great campaign and again marched against Zhongli, Puhui served as Chief Clerk to the Separate Commander under Prince Anle, Yuan Quan.

sentences.zh: 班師，除揚烈將軍、相州安北府司馬。

translations.literal: After the army withdrew, he was appointed General Who Displays Majesty and Army Aide of the Northern Pacification Headquarters in Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew, he was appointed General Who Displays Majesty and Army Aide of the Northern Pacification Headquarters in Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 後以本官領河南尹丞。

translations.literal: Later, retaining his original office, he served concurrently as Assistant to the Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while retaining his original office, he served concurrently as Assistant to the Administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，坐與甄楷等飲酒遊從，免官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, he was dismissed from office for drinking and carousing with Zhen Kai and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, he was dismissed from office for drinking and carousing with Zhen Kai and others.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍刁整，家有舊訓，將營儉葬。

translations.literal: General of Valiant Cavalry Diao Zheng, whose family had an old instruction, was about to arrange a frugal burial.
translations.idiomatic: General of Valiant Cavalry Diao Zheng, whose family had an old instruction, was about to arrange a frugal burial.

sentences.zh: 普惠以為矯時太甚，與整書論之。

translations.literal: Puhui thought this was excessively bending to the fashion of the times and wrote Diao Zheng a letter arguing the point.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui thought this bent too far to the fashion of the times and wrote Diao Zheng a letter arguing the point.

sentences.zh: 事在刁雍傳。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the biography of Diao Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in the biography of Diao Yong.

sentences.zh: 故事：免官者，三載之後降一階而敍，若才優擢授，不拘此限。

translations.literal: Precedent: those dismissed from office, after three years, had their rank reduced one grade upon reappointment; but if talent was outstanding, promotion was not bound by this limit.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent held that those dismissed from office, after three years, had their rank reduced one grade upon reappointment. But if talent was outstanding, promotion was not bound by this limit.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，吏部尚書李韶奏普惠有文學，依才優之例，宜特顯敍，敕除寧遠將軍、司空倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: During the Xiping era, Minister of the Interior Li Shao memorialized that Puhui had literary learning and, following the precedent for outstanding talent, ought to receive a special conspicuous reappointment; by edict he was appointed General of Distant Pacification and Army Clerk of the Granary Bureau under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era, Minister of the Interior Li Shao memorialized that Puhui had literary learning and, following the precedent for outstanding talent, ought to receive a special conspicuous reappointment. By edict he was appointed General of Distant Pacification and Army Clerk of the Granary Bureau under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 朝議以不降階為榮。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that not having one's rank reduced was an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion held that not having one's rank reduced was an honor.

sentences.zh: 時任城王澄為司空，表議書記，多出普惠。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Cheng of Rencheng served as Minister of Works; drafts for memorials and deliberations mostly came from Puhui.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Cheng of Rencheng served as Minister of Works, drafts for memorials and deliberations mostly came from Puhui.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王恭、北海王顥，疑為所生祖母服期與三年，博士執意不同，詔羣僚會議。

translations.literal: Princes Gong of Guangling and Hao of Beihai questioned whether the mourning period for their biological grandmothers should match the three-year term. The Erudites held conflicting views, and an edict ordered the assembled officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Gong of Guangling and Hao of Beihai questioned whether the mourning period for their biological grandmothers should match the three-year term. The Erudites held conflicting views, and an edict ordered the assembled officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 普惠議曰：「謹按二王祖母，皆受命先朝，為二國太妃，可謂受命於天子，為始封之母矣。

translations.literal: Puhui argued: "I respectfully consider that the grandmothers of both princes received their appointments from the former court and served as Grand Consorts of two states — they may be said to have received their charge from the Son of Heaven and to have been the founding mothers of those fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui argued: "I respectfully consider that the grandmothers of both princes received their appointments from the former court and served as Grand Consorts of two states. They may be said to have received their charge from the Son of Heaven and to have been the founding mothers of those fiefs.

sentences.zh: 喪服『慈母如母』，在三年章。

translations.literal: In the Mourning Garments, "a nurturing mother is treated as a mother" appears in the chapter on three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Mourning Garments, "a nurturing mother is treated as a mother" appears in the chapter on three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『貴父命也。』

translations.literal: The commentary says: "This honors the father's command."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "This honors the father's command."

sentences.zh: 鄭注云：『大夫之妾子，父在為母大功，則士之妾子為母期。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says: 'For a great officer's son by a concubine, while the father lives he wears second-grade mourning for his mother; then for a serviceman's son by a concubine it is one-year mourning for his mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says: "For a great officer's son by a concubine, while the father lives he wears second-grade mourning for his mother; for a serviceman's son by a concubine, it is one-year mourning for his mother."

sentences.zh: 父卒則皆得申。』

translations.literal: When the father dies, both may extend their mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the father dies, both may extend their mourning.

sentences.zh: 此大夫命其妾子，以為母所慈，猶曰貴父命，為之三年，況天子命其子為列國王，命其所生母為國太妃，反自同公子為母練冠之與大功乎？

translations.literal: This is a great officer commanding his son by a concubine; because the mother nurtured him, still honoring the father's command one wears three-year mourning for her — how much the more when the Son of Heaven appoints his son king of a feudal state and appoints the prince's biological mother Grand Consort of the state, yet one would instead equate this with a prince's son wearing the dyed cap or second-grade mourning for his mother?
translations.idiomatic: Here a great officer commands his son by a concubine; because the mother nurtured him, one still honors the father's command and wears three-year mourning for her. How much more so when the Son of Heaven appoints his son king of a feudal state and appoints the prince's biological mother Grand Consort of the state — yet one would equate this with a prince's son wearing the dyed cap or second-grade mourning for his mother?

sentences.zh: 輕重顛倒，不可之甚者也。

translations.literal: Light and heavy inverted — there could be no greater error.
translations.idiomatic: Light and heavy inverted — there could be no greater error.

sentences.zh: 傳曰，『始封之君，不臣諸父昆弟』，則當服其親服。

translations.literal: The commentary says, 'The first enfeoffed lord does not treat his father's brothers and own brothers as subjects' — therefore one ought to wear mourning according to the kinship grade.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "The first enfeoffed lord does not treat his father's brothers and own brothers as subjects." Therefore one ought to wear mourning according to the kinship grade.

sentences.zh: 若魯衞列國，相為服期，判無疑矣。

translations.literal: If it were feudal states like Lu and Wei, wearing one-year mourning for each other would clearly be beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If it were feudal states like Lu and Wei, wearing one-year mourning for each other would clearly be beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How may this be demonstrated?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be demonstrated?

sentences.zh: 喪服，『君為姑姊妹女子嫁於國君者』，傳曰：『何以大功？

translations.literal: In Mourning Garments, 'For the lord's father's sisters and the women of his clan married to feudal lords,' the commentary says: 'Why second-grade mourning?'
translations.idiomatic: In Mourning Garments, "For the lord's father's sisters and the women of his clan married to feudal lords," the commentary asks: "Why second-grade mourning?"

sentences.zh: 尊同也。

translations.literal: Because their ranks are equal.
translations.idiomatic: Because their ranks are equal.

sentences.zh: 尊同，則得服其親服。

translations.literal: When ranks are equal, one may wear mourning according to the kinship grade.
translations.idiomatic: When ranks are equal, one may wear mourning according to the kinship grade.

sentences.zh: 諸侯之子稱公子，公子不得禰先君。』

translations.literal: A feudal lord's son is called a prince; a prince may not enshrine the former lord in his temple.
translations.idiomatic: A feudal lord's son is called a prince; a prince may not enshrine the former lord in his temple.

sentences.zh: 然則兄弟一體。

translations.literal: Therefore brothers are of one body.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore brothers are of one body.

sentences.zh: 位列諸侯，自以尊同得相為服，不可還準公子，遠厭天王。

translations.literal: Once ranked as feudal lords, they by virtue of equal rank may wear mourning for one another; one cannot still apply the standard of a prince and apply distant reduction toward the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Once ranked among the feudal lords, they by virtue of equal rank may wear mourning for one another. One cannot still apply the standard of a prince and apply distant reduction toward the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故降有四品，君、大夫以尊降，公子、大夫之子以厭降。

translations.literal: Therefore there are four grades of reduction: lords and great officers reduce by rank, princes and great officers' sons reduce by surfeit.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore there are four grades of reduction: lords and great officers reduce by rank; princes and great officers' sons reduce by surfeit.

sentences.zh: 名例不同，何可亂也。

translations.literal: The categories differ in name and rule — how can they be confused?
translations.idiomatic: The categories differ in name and rule — how can they be confused?

sentences.zh: 禮，大夫之妾子，以父命慈己，申其三年。

translations.literal: By ritual, a great officer's son by a concubine, because the father commanded that he be nurtured, extends to three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, a great officer's son by a concubine, because the father commanded that he be nurtured, extends to three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 太妃既受命先帝，光昭一國，二王胙土茅社，顯錫大邦，舍尊同之高據，附不禰之公子，雖許蔡失位，亦不是過。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort already received her appointment from the former emperor, her honor illuminating an entire state; the two princes were granted fiefs with earth and ceremonial insignia, conspicuously bestowed great domains — to abandon the high ground of equal rank and attach oneself to the category of a prince who cannot enshrine his ancestor, even the loss of status of Xu and Cai would not be excessive.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Consort already received her appointment from the former emperor, her honor illuminating an entire state. The two princes were granted fiefs with earth and ceremonial insignia, conspicuously bestowed great domains. To abandon the high ground of equal rank and attach oneself to the category of a prince who cannot enshrine his ancestor — even the demotion of Xu and Cai would not be excessive.

sentences.zh: 服問曰：『有從輕而重，公子之妻為其皇姑。』

translations.literal: Mourning Questions says: 'There are cases where mourning goes from light to heavy: a prince's wife for her imperial mother-in-law.'
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Questions says: "There are cases where mourning goes from light to heavy: a prince's wife for her imperial mother-in-law."

sentences.zh: 公子雖厭，妻尚獲申，況廣陵、北海，論封則封君之子，語妃則命妃之孫。

translations.literal: Though a prince is subject to surfeit reduction, his wife may still extend her mourning — how much the more for Guangling and Beihai: speaking of their fiefs they are sons of enfeoffed lords; speaking of the Grand Consort they are grandsons of the appointed consort.
translations.idiomatic: Though a prince is subject to surfeit reduction, his wife may still extend her mourning. How much more for Guangling and Beihai: speaking of their fiefs they are sons of enfeoffed lords; speaking of the Grand Consort they are grandsons of the appointed consort.

sentences.zh: 承妃纂重，遠別先皇，更以先后之正統，厭其所生之祖嫡，方之皇姑，不以遙乎？

translations.literal: Inheriting the Grand Consort's weighty succession, distantly separated from the late emperor, yet further applying the orthodox line of the empress to suppress mourning for the biological grandmother's full relation — compared to the imperial mother-in-law, is this not even more remote?
translations.idiomatic: Inheriting the Grand Consort's weighty succession, distantly separated from the late emperor, yet further applying the orthodox line of the empress to suppress mourning for the biological grandmother's full relation — compared to the imperial mother-in-law, is this not even more remote?

sentences.zh: 今既許其申服，而復限之以期，比之慈母，不亦爽歟！

translations.literal: Now that extension of mourning is granted, yet it is again limited to one year — compared to a nurturing mother, is this not contradictory!
translations.idiomatic: Now that extension of mourning is granted, yet it is again limited to one year — compared to a nurturing mother, is this not contradictory!

sentences.zh: 經曰，『為君之祖父母父母妻長子』，傳曰：『何以期？

translations.literal: The canon says, 'For the lord's grandparents, parents, and wife's eldest son,' the commentary says: 'Why one year?'
translations.idiomatic: The canon says: "For the lord's grandparents, parents, and wife's eldest son." The commentary asks: "Why one year?"

sentences.zh: 父母長子君服斬，妻則小君。

translations.literal: The lord's parents and eldest son wear highest mourning; the wife is the lesser lord.
translations.idiomatic: The lord's parents and eldest son wear highest mourning; the wife is the lesser lord.

sentences.zh: 父卒，然後為祖後者服斬。』

translations.literal: When the father dies, then the heir of the grandfather wears highest mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the father dies, then the heir of the grandfather wears highest mourning.

sentences.zh: 今祖乃獻文皇帝，諸侯不得祖之，母為太妃，蓋二王三年之證。

translations.literal: Now the grandfather is Emperor Xianwen — feudal lords cannot enshrine him as ancestor; their mother is Grand Consort — this is surely proof of the two princes' three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Now the grandfather is Emperor Xianwen — feudal lords cannot enshrine him as ancestor. Their mother is Grand Consort — this is surely proof of the two princes' three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 議者近背正經以附非類，差之毫毛，所失或遠。

translations.literal: Those in the debate lately abandon the orthodox canon to attach themselves to improper categories — a hair's breadth of error may lead to far-reaching loss.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the debate lately abandon the orthodox canon to attach themselves to improper categories. A hair's breadth of error may lead to far-reaching loss.

sentences.zh: 且天子尊則配天，莫非臣妾，何為命之為國母而不聽子服其親乎？

translations.literal: Moreover when the Son of Heaven is supreme he matches Heaven — all are his subjects; why appoint her Grand Consort of the state yet not allow the sons to mourn their kin as kin?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the Son of Heaven is supreme he matches Heaven — all are his subjects. Why appoint her Grand Consort of the state yet not allow the sons to mourn their kin as kin?

sentences.zh: 記曰：『從服者，所從亡，則已。』

translations.literal: The Record says: 'For derivative mourning, when the one followed is gone, it ceases.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "For derivative mourning, when the one followed is gone, it ceases."

sentences.zh: 又曰：不為君母之黨服，則為其母之黨服。

translations.literal: It also says: If one does not mourn the lord's mother's kinsmen, then one mourns one's own mother's kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: If one does not mourn the lord's mother's kinsmen, then one mourns one's own mother's kinsmen.

sentences.zh: [3]今所從既亡，不以親服服其所生，則屬從之服於何所施？

translations.literal: [3] Now that the one followed is gone, if one does not wear kin mourning for the biological relation, then to what is derivative mourning to be applied?
translations.idiomatic: [3] Now that the one followed is gone, if one does not wear kin mourning for the biological relation, then to what is derivative mourning to be applied?

sentences.zh: 若以諸王入為公卿，便同大夫者，則當今之議，皆不須以國為言也。

translations.literal: If princes entering office as high ministers were treated the same as great officers, then in the present debate there would be no need to speak in terms of feudal states at all.
translations.idiomatic: If princes entering office as high ministers were treated the same as great officers, then in the present debate there would be no need to speak in terms of feudal states at all.

sentences.zh: 今之諸王，自同列國，雖不之國，別置臣僚，玉食一方，不得以諸侯言之。

translations.literal: Today's princes are themselves equivalent to feudal states; though they do not go to their domains, they separately appoint officials and ministers, enjoy the bounty of a region — they cannot be discussed simply as 'feudal lords.'
translations.idiomatic: Today's princes are themselves equivalent to feudal states. Though they do not go to their domains, they separately appoint officials and ministers and enjoy the bounty of a region — they cannot be discussed simply as feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 敢據周禮，輒同三年。」

translations.literal: I dare rely on the Zhou Rites and apply the same three-year mourning."
translations.idiomatic: I dare rely on the Zhou Rites and apply the same three-year mourning."

sentences.zh: 當時議者亦有同異。

translations.literal: Among those debating at the time there were also agreements and disagreements.
translations.idiomatic: Among those debating at the time there were also agreements and disagreements.

sentences.zh: 國子博士李郁於議罷之後，書難普惠。

translations.literal: After the debate concluded, Imperial University Erudite Li Yu wrote challenging Puhui.
