translations.idiomatic: After the debate concluded, Imperial University Erudite Li Yu wrote challenging Puhui.

sentences.zh: 普惠據禮還答，鄭重三返，郁議遂屈。

translations.literal: Puhui replied on the basis of ritual, seriously three times in succession; Li Yu's argument was thus defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui replied on the basis of ritual, seriously and three times in succession; Li Yu's argument was thus defeated.

sentences.zh: 轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Remonstrating Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Remonstrating Advisor.

sentences.zh: 澄謂普惠曰：「不喜君得諫議，唯喜諫議得君。」

translations.literal: Cheng said to Puhui: "I do not rejoice that you obtained Remonstrating Advisor; I only rejoice that Remonstrating Advisor obtained you."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said to Puhui: "I do not rejoice that you obtained Remonstrating Advisor; I only rejoice that Remonstrating Advisor obtained you."

sentences.zh: 臣聞優名寶位，王者之所光錫；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that excellent titles and honored ranks are what the king lavishly bestows;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that excellent titles and honored ranks are what the king lavishly bestows;

sentences.zh: 尊君愛親，臣子所以慎終。

translations.literal: honoring the lord and cherishing kin are how ministers and sons see duty through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: honoring the lord and cherishing kin are how ministers and sons see duty through to the end.

sentences.zh: 必使勳績相侔，號秩相可，然後能顯揚當時，傳徽萬代者矣。

translations.literal: Merit and achievement must be matched, titles and ranks must be fitting — only then can one glorify the present age and transmit luster through ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and achievement must be matched, titles and ranks must be fitting — only then can one glorify the present age and transmit luster through ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 竊見故侍中、司徒胡公，懷道含靈，實誕聖后，載育至尊，母儀四海，近樞克唯允之寄，居槐體論道之明。

translations.literal: I have observed the late Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works Duke Hu: he embraced the Way and bore spiritual virtue, truly the one who gave birth to the Sacred Empress, who nurtured the Supreme Sovereign, whose maternal example filled the four seas; near the pivot he fulfilled the charge of sole trust, and in the Ministry of Works embodied the clarity of discourse on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed the late Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works Duke Hu: he embraced the Way and bore spiritual virtue, truly the one who gave birth to the Sacred Empress, who nurtured the Supreme Sovereign, whose maternal example filled the four seas. Near the pivot of power he fulfilled the charge of sole trust, and as Minister of Works embodied the clarity of discourse on the Way.

sentences.zh: 故以功餘九錫，褒假鑾纛，深聖上之加隆，極慈后之至愛，憲章天下，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Therefore, with merit beyond the Nine Bestowals, honored with imperial regalia and battle standards, deeply exalted by the Sacred Sovereign, and receiving the utmost love of the Benevolent Empress — to proclaim this as law throughout the realm, would that not be fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, with merit beyond the Nine Bestowals, honored with imperial regalia and battle standards, deeply exalted by the Sacred Sovereign and receiving the utmost love of the Benevolent Empress — to proclaim this as law throughout the realm, would that not be fitting?

sentences.zh: 而「太上」之號，竊謂未衷。

translations.literal: Yet the title "Supreme" — I respectfully consider it not yet apt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the title "Supreme" — I respectfully consider it not yet apt.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 易稱：「天尊地卑，乾坤定矣。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven is lofty and earth is lowly — thus Qian and Kun are fixed."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Heaven is lofty and earth is lowly — thus Qian and Kun are fixed."

sentences.zh: 故曰「大哉乾元」，又曰「至哉坤元」。

translations.literal: Therefore it says "How great is the primal power of Qian," and again "How perfect is the primal power of Kun."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it says "How great is the primal power of Qian," and again "How perfect is the primal power of Kun."

sentences.zh: 明乾坤不可並大。

translations.literal: This shows that Qian and Kun cannot both be supreme.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that Qian and Kun cannot both be supreme.

sentences.zh: 禮記曰：「天無二日，土無二王。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: "Heaven has no second sun; earth has no second king.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: "Heaven has no second sun; earth has no second king.

sentences.zh: 嘗禘郊社，尊無二上。」

translations.literal: At the seasonal sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, honor admits no second apex."
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, honor admits no second apex."

sentences.zh: 明君臣不可並上。

translations.literal: This shows that lord and minister cannot both stand at the apex.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that lord and minister cannot both stand at the apex.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書，以司徒為太上秦公，夫人為太上秦君。

translations.literal: I have seen in the edict that the Minister of Works is styled Supreme Duke of Qin, and his lady Supreme Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen in the edict that the Minister of Works is styled Supreme Duke of Qin, and his lady Supreme Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 夫人蒙號於前，司徒繫之於後，尊光之美盛矣。

translations.literal: The lady received her title first, the Minister of Works was attached afterward — the splendor of honor is indeed magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: The lady received her title first, the Minister of Works was attached afterward — the splendor of honor is indeed magnificent.

sentences.zh: 竊惟高祖受禪於獻文皇帝，故仰尊為太上皇，此因上上而生名也。

translations.literal: I consider that Emperor Gaozu received the abdication from Emperor Xianwen, and therefore raised him in honor as Supreme Emperor — this title arose from the supreme one above the supreme.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Emperor Gaozu received the abdication from Emperor Xianwen, and therefore raised him in honor as Supreme Emperor — this title arose from the supreme one above the supreme.

sentences.zh: 皇太后稱令以繫敕下，蓋取三從之道，遠同文母，列於十亂，則司徒之為太上，恐乖繫敕之意。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager uses the term "Order" to attach her commands below — this takes the way of the three followings, far matching Wen Mu, ranked among the Ten Disordered; then for the Minister of Works to be styled Supreme — I fear this goes against the intent of attaching commands below.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager uses the term "Order" to attach her commands below — this takes the way of the three followings, far matching Wen Mu, ranked among the Ten Disordered. For the Minister of Works to be styled Supreme — I fear this goes against the intent of attaching commands below.

sentences.zh: 春秋傳曰：葬稱公，臣子辭。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn commentary says: At burial one styles him Duke — the minister and son declines.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn commentary says: At burial one styles him Duke — the minister and son declines.

sentences.zh: 明不可復加上也。

translations.literal: This shows that one cannot add further titles.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that one cannot add further titles.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「茲予大饗于先王，爾祖其從與饗之。」

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Now I shall greatly feast at the former kings — may your ancestor follow and share in the feast."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "Now I shall greatly feast at the former kings — may your ancestor follow and share in the feast."

sentences.zh: 司徒位尊屬重，必當配饗先朝，稱太上以為臣，以事太上皇，恐非司徒翼翼之心。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works' rank is lofty and his relation weighty — he must surely share in the sacrificial feast of the former court. To style him Supreme yet treat him as a minister, serving the Supreme Emperor — I fear this is not what the Minister of Works earnestly desired in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works' rank is lofty and his relation weighty — he must surely share in the sacrificial feast of the former court. To style him Supreme yet treat him as a minister serving the Supreme Emperor — I fear this is not what the Minister of Works earnestly desired in his heart.

sentences.zh: 漢祖創有天下，尊父曰「太上皇」，母曰「昭靈后」，乃帝者之事。

translations.literal: The Founder of Han created the realm and honored his father as "Supreme Emperor" and his mother as "Empress Zhao Ling" — these are matters for emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder of Han created the realm and honored his father as "Supreme Emperor" and his mother as "Empress Zhao Ling" — these are matters for emperors.

sentences.zh: 晉有「小子侯」，尚曰僭之於天子。

translations.literal: In Jin there was the "Lesser Son Marquis" — even so it was said to usurp the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin there was the "Lesser Son Marquis" — even so it was said to usurp the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 司徒，三公也，其可同號於帝乎？

translations.literal: The Minister of Works is one of the Three Dukes — how can he share the same title as an emperor?
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works is one of the Three Dukes — how can he share the same title as an emperor?

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「必也正名，名不正則言不順，言不順則事不成，事不成則禮樂不興，禮樂不興則刑罰不中，刑罰不中則民無所措手足。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "One must rectify names. If names are not correct, speech will not be in order; if speech is not in order, affairs will not succeed; if affairs do not succeed, rites and music will not flourish; if rites and music do not flourish, punishments will not hit the mark; if punishments do not hit the mark, the people will have nowhere to set hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "One must rectify names. If names are not correct, speech will not be in order; if speech is not in order, affairs will not succeed; if affairs do not succeed, rites and music will not flourish; if rites and music do not flourish, punishments will not hit the mark; if punishments do not hit the mark, the people will have nowhere to set hand or foot."

sentences.zh: 易曰「有大者不可以盈，故受之以謙」，「謙尊而光，卑而不可踰」，「天道虧盈而益謙，地道變盈而流謙，鬼神害盈而福謙，人道惡盈而好謙」。

translations.literal: The Changes says "When one who is great cannot be filled, therefore Humility follows," "Humility: honored yet radiant, lowly yet not to be overstepped," "The Way of Heaven diminishes the full and benefits the humble; the Way of Earth transforms the full and pours into the humble; ghosts and spirits harm the full and bless the humble; the Way of Man hates the full and loves the humble."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "When one who is great cannot be filled, therefore Humility follows." "Humility: honored yet radiant, lowly yet not to be overstepped." "The Way of Heaven diminishes the full and benefits the humble; the Way of Earth transforms the full and pours into the humble; ghosts and spirits harm the full and bless the humble; the Way of Man hates the full and loves the humble."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「困於上者必反於下，故受之以井。」

translations.literal: It also says: "One trapped above must turn back below — therefore the Well follows."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "One trapped above must turn back below — therefore the Well follows."

sentences.zh: 比剋吉定兆，而以淺改卜，羣心悲惋，亦或天地神靈所以垂至戒，啟聖情。

translations.literal: Recently a propitious site was chosen and the omen fixed, yet the burial was changed to a shallower location — the hearts of the multitude grieved and lamented. Perhaps this too is how Heaven and Earth and the spirits show their utmost warning and awaken the Sacred One's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a propitious site was chosen and the omen fixed, yet the burial was changed to a shallower location — the hearts of the multitude grieved and lamented. Perhaps this too is how Heaven and Earth and the spirits show their utmost warning and awaken the Sacred One's feelings.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖后回日月之明，察微臣之請，停司徒逼同之號，從卑下不踰之稱，畏困上之鑒，邀謙光之福，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that the Sacred Empress would turn back the brilliance of sun and moon, examine this humble servant's plea, halt the Minister of Works' forced equal title, follow the designation that is lowly and not to be overstepped, fear the warning of being trapped above, and seek the blessing of radiant humility — then the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish that the Sacred Empress would turn back the brilliance of sun and moon, examine this humble servant's plea, halt the Minister of Works' forced equal title, follow the designation that is lowly and not to be overstepped, fear the warning of being trapped above, and seek the blessing of radiant humility — then the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 臣聞見災修德，災變成善。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when one sees calamity one cultivates virtue, and calamity turns into good.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when one sees calamity one cultivates virtue, and calamity turns into good.

sentences.zh: 此太戊所以興殷，桑穀以之自滅。

translations.literal: This is why Tai Jia revived Yin, and why Sang Gu perished by it.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Tai Jia revived Yin, and why Sang Gu perished by it.

sentences.zh: 況今卜遷方始，當修革之會，愚以為無上之名，不可假之，脫譏於千載，恐貽不言之咎。

translations.literal: Moreover, now that the divination for relocation has just begun, at a moment when reform ought to be undertaken — I am of the view that the title of "none above" cannot be lent out; if one invites ridicule for a thousand years, I fear one will incur blame that cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, now that the divination for relocation has just begun, at a moment when reform ought to be undertaken — I am of the view that the title of "none above" cannot be lent out. If one invites ridicule for a thousand years, I fear one will incur blame that cannot be spoken.

sentences.zh: 且君之於臣，比葬三臨之，禮也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a lord faces a minister at burial, he thrice attends in person — this is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a lord faces a minister at burial, he thrice attends in person — this is ritual.

sentences.zh: 司徒誠為后父，實人臣也。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works is indeed the empress's father, but in truth he is a subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works is indeed the empress's father, but in truth he is a subject.

sentences.zh: 雖子尊不加於父，乃天下母以義斷恩，不可遂在室之意，故曰「女子有行，遠父母兄弟」。

translations.literal: Though a son's honor does not exceed his father's, as Mother of the Realm she must sever affection by righteousness and cannot indulge the feelings of one still in her maiden home — hence it is said "When a woman has a destination, she is distant from parents and brothers."
translations.idiomatic: Though a son's honor does not exceed his father's, as Mother of the Realm she must sever affection by righteousness and cannot indulge the feelings of one still in her maiden home — hence it is said: "When a woman has a destination, she is distant from parents and brothers."

sentences.zh: 況乃應坤之載，承天之重，而朔望於司徒之殯，晨昏於郊墓之間，雖聖思蒸蒸，其不虞宜戒。

translations.literal: How much more when she bears the burden of Kun and carries the weight of Heaven — yet at the new and full moon attends the Minister of Works' bier, morning and evening between the suburban tombs; though the Sacred One's thoughts are warm and earnest, ought one not guard against the unforeseen?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when she bears the burden of Kun and carries the weight of Heaven — yet at the new and full moon attends the Minister of Works' bier, morning and evening between the suburban tombs. Though the Sacred One's thoughts are warm and earnest, ought one not guard against the unforeseen?

sentences.zh: 離宸極之嚴居，疲雲蹕於道路，此亦億兆蒼生，瞻仰失圖。

translations.literal: Leaving the strict abode of the imperial pole, exhausting the imperial escort on the roads — this too is the myriad masses looking up and losing their compass.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the strict abode of the imperial pole, exhausting the imperial escort on the roads — this too is the myriad masses looking up and losing their compass.

sentences.zh: 伏願尋載馳之不歸，存靜方之光大，則草木可繁，人靈斯穆。

translations.literal: I humbly wish you would recall how the carriage that raced forth did not return, and preserve the radiance of stillness and rectitude — then vegetation may flourish and the people's spirits will be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish you would recall how the carriage that raced forth did not return, and preserve the radiance of stillness and rectitude — then vegetation may flourish and the people's spirits will be at peace.

sentences.zh: 臣職忝諫司，敢獻狂瞽，謹冒上聞，不敢宣露，乞垂省覽，昭臣微款，脫得奉謁聖顏，曲盡愚衷者，死且不朽。

translations.literal: Your servant's office disgraces the remonstrance bureau; I dare offer this reckless blindness, respectfully presume to report upward, and dare not disclose it openly. I beg you to examine it, make clear this humble servant's sincere intent — if I may be granted audience with the Sacred Countenance and fully express my foolish loyalty, I would die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's office disgraces the remonstrance bureau; I dare offer this reckless blindness and respectfully presume to report upward, yet dare not disclose it openly. I beg you to examine it and make clear this humble servant's sincere intent. If I may be granted audience with the Sacred Countenance and fully express my foolish loyalty, I would die without regret.

sentences.zh: 太后覽表，親至國珍宅，召集王公、八座、卿尹及五品已上，博議其事，遣使召普惠與相問答，又令侍中元叉、中常侍賈璨監觀得失。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager read the memorial, personally went to Hu Guozhen's residence, summoned princes, the Eight Seats, ministers and administrators, and all of fifth rank and above, broadly deliberated the matter, sent envoys to summon Puhui for mutual questioning and answering, and further ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Cha and Palace Attendant Jia Can to supervise and observe gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager read the memorial, personally went to Hu Guozhen's residence, summoned princes, the Eight Seats, ministers and administrators, and all of fifth rank and above to broadly deliberate the matter. She sent envoys to summon Puhui for mutual questioning and answering, and further ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Cha and Palace Attendant Jia Can to supervise and observe gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄問普惠曰：「漢高作帝，尊父為太上皇。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng asked Puhui: "When Emperor Gaozu of Han became emperor, he honored his father as Supreme Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng asked Puhui: "When Emperor Gaozu of Han became emperor, he honored his father as Supreme Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今聖母臨朝，贈父太上公，求之故實，非為無準。

translations.literal: Now the Sacred Mother holds court and posthumously honors her father as Supreme Duke — searching ancient precedents, this is not without standard.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Sacred Mother holds court and posthumously honors her father as Supreme Duke — searching ancient precedents, this is not without standard.

sentences.zh: 且君舉作則，何必循舊。」

translations.literal: Moreover when the lord acts, he establishes the norm — why must one follow the old?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the lord acts, he establishes the norm — why must one follow the old?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天子稱詔，太后稱令，故周臣十亂，文母預焉。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Son of Heaven styles his words Edict; the Empress Dowager styles hers Order — therefore among the Zhou ministers in the Ten Disordered, Wen Mu participated.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The Son of Heaven styles his words Edict; the Empress Dowager styles hers Order — therefore among the Zhou ministers in the Ten Disordered, Wen Mu participated.

sentences.zh: 仰思所難，竊謂非匹。」

translations.literal: Looking up and pondering what is difficult, I respectfully consider it not a match."
translations.idiomatic: Looking up and pondering what is difficult, I respectfully consider it not a match."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「前代太后亦有稱詔，聖母自欲存謙光之義，故不稱耳，何得以詔令之別，而廢嚴父之孝？」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Former empresses dowager also styled their words Edict; the Sacred Mother herself wished to preserve the meaning of radiant humility, and therefore did not style them so — how can one, on the basis of the Edict-Order distinction, abandon filial piety toward one's stern father?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said: "Former empresses dowager also styled their words Edict. The Sacred Mother herself wished to preserve the meaning of radiant humility, and therefore did not style them so. How can one, on the basis of the Edict-Order distinction, abandon filial piety toward one's stern father?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「后父太上，自昔未有。

translations.literal: He replied: "An empress's father styled Supreme — from antiquity there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "An empress's father styled Supreme — from antiquity there has never been such a thing.

sentences.zh: 前代母后豈不欲尊崇其親，王何以不遠謨古義，而近順今旨。

translations.literal: Did former empresses dowager not wish to honor their kin? Why does Your Highness not consult distant ancient meaning, but instead closely follow the present intent?
translations.idiomatic: Did former empresses dowager not wish to honor their kin? Why does Your Highness not consult distant ancient meaning, but instead closely follow the present intent?

sentences.zh: 未審太后何故謙於稱詔，而不謙於太上。

translations.literal: I do not understand why the Empress Dowager was humble in styling Edict, yet not humble regarding Supreme.
translations.idiomatic: I do not understand why the Empress Dowager was humble in styling Edict, yet not humble regarding Supreme.

sentences.zh: 竊願聖后終其謙光。」

translations.literal: I respectfully wish the Sacred Empress would carry her radiant humility through to the end."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully wish the Sacred Empress would carry her radiant humility through to the end."

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌曰：「昔在僭晉，褚氏臨朝，殷浩遺褚裒書曰『足下，今之太上皇也』，況太上公而致疑。」

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe said: "Formerly under usurping Jin, the Chu clan held court; Yin Hao sent Chu Pou a letter saying 'You, sir, are today's Supreme Emperor' — how much more Supreme Duke, yet you raise doubts."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe said: "Formerly under usurping Jin, the Chu clan held court. Yin Hao sent Chu Pou a letter saying 'You, sir, are today's Supreme Emperor' — how much more Supreme Duke, yet you raise doubts."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「褚裒以女輔政辭不入朝。

translations.literal: He replied: "Chu Pou, because his daughter assisted in government, declined to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Chu Pou, because his daughter assisted in government, declined to enter court.

sentences.zh: 淵源譏其不恭，故有太上之刺。

translations.literal: Huan Yuan mocked his lack of respect — therefore there was the barb of Supreme.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yuan mocked his lack of respect — therefore there was the barb of Supreme.

sentences.zh: 本稱其非，不記其是。

translations.literal: It originally marked his fault, not recorded his correctness.
translations.idiomatic: It originally marked his fault, not recorded his correctness.

sentences.zh: 不謂殿下以此賜難。」

translations.literal: I did not expect Your Highness to use this as a challenge."
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect Your Highness to use this as a challenge."

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光曰：「張生表中引晉有小子侯，出自鄭注，非為正經。」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang said: "In Scholar Zhang's memorial he cites Jin's Lesser Son Marquis — this comes from Zheng's commentary and is not the orthodox canon."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang said: "In Scholar Zhang's memorial he cites Jin's Lesser Son Marquis — this comes from Zheng's commentary and is not the orthodox canon."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「雖非正經之文，然述正經之旨。

translations.literal: He replied: "Though it is not text of the orthodox canon, it yet expounds the orthodox canon's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Though it is not text of the orthodox canon, it yet expounds the orthodox canon's intent.

sentences.zh: 公好古習禮，復固斯難？」

translations.literal: You love antiquity and study ritual — will you again stubbornly raise this challenge?"
translations.idiomatic: You love antiquity and study ritual — will you again stubbornly raise this challenge?"

sentences.zh: 御史中尉元匡因謂崔光曰：「張表云，晉之小子侯，以號同稱僭。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang thereupon said to Cui Guang: "Scholar Zhang's memorial says that Jin's Lesser Son Marquis was deemed usurpation because the title was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang thereupon said to Cui Guang: "Scholar Zhang's memorial says that Jin's Lesser Son Marquis was deemed usurpation because the title was the same.

sentences.zh: 今者，太上公名同太上皇，比晉小子，義似相類。

translations.literal: Now the title Supreme Duke is the same as Supreme Emperor — compared to Jin's Lesser Son, the meaning seems similar.
translations.idiomatic: Now the title Supreme Duke is the same as Supreme Emperor — compared to Jin's Lesser Son, the meaning seems similar.

sentences.zh: 但不學不敢辨其是非。」

translations.literal: But lacking learning, I dare not distinguish right from wrong."
translations.idiomatic: But lacking learning, I dare not distinguish right from wrong."

sentences.zh: 普惠對曰：「中丞既疑其是，不正其非，豈所望於三獨。」

translations.literal: Puhui replied: "Since the Censor-in-Chief already suspects it is correct, why not correct what is wrong — is this what is expected of one of the Three Solitary Remonstrators?"
translations.idiomatic: Puhui replied: "Since the Censor-in-Chief already suspects it is correct, why not correct what is wrong — is this what is expected of one of the Three Solitary Remonstrators?"

sentences.zh: 尚書崔亮曰：「諫議所見，正以太上之號不應施於人臣。

translations.literal: Minister of the Household Cui Liang said: "The Remonstrance Counselor's view is precisely that the title Supreme should not be applied to a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Household Cui Liang said: "The Remonstrance Counselor is right — the title Supreme ought not be bestowed on a minister.

sentences.zh: 然周有太公尚父，亦兼二名。

translations.literal: Yet in Zhou there was Grand Duke Father Venerable, who also combined two names.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zhou had the Grand Duke called Father Venerable — he bore two honorifics at once.

sentences.zh: 人臣尊重之稱，固知非始今日。」

translations.literal: Honorific titles for ministers — one surely knows this did not begin only today."
translations.idiomatic: Respectful titles for ministers are nothing new, as everyone knows."

sentences.zh: 普惠對曰：「尚父者，有德可尚；

translations.literal: Puhui replied: "Father Venerable — one has virtue that can be venerated;
translations.idiomatic: Puhui replied: "'Father Venerable' means virtue worthy of reverence;

sentences.zh: 太上者，上中之上。

translations.literal: Supreme — supreme among the supreme.
translations.idiomatic: "Supreme" means the highest of the high.

sentences.zh: 名同義異，此亦非並。」

translations.literal: The names are alike but the meanings differ — this too is not an equivalence."
translations.idiomatic: The words may sound alike, but their meaning is not the same — these cannot be lumped together."

sentences.zh: 亮又曰：「古有文王、武王，亦有文子、武子。

translations.literal: Liang again said: "In antiquity there were King Wen and King Wu, and also Wenzi and Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang went on: "Ancient times had King Wen and King Wu — and also sons styled Wenzi and Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 然則，太上皇、太上公亦何嫌其同也？」

translations.literal: If so, what objection is there to Supreme Emperor and Supreme Duke sharing the same word?"
translations.idiomatic: By that logic, what harm if Supreme Emperor and Supreme Duke share the same prefix?"

sentences.zh: 普惠對曰：「文武者，德行之迹，故迹同則諡同。

translations.literal: Puhui replied: "Wen and Wu are traces of virtue and conduct — therefore when the traces are alike, the posthumous names are alike.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui replied: "'Wen' and 'Wu' denote deeds of virtue — when the deeds match, the posthumous epithets match.

sentences.zh: 太上者，尊極之位，豈得通施於臣下！」

translations.literal: Supreme is a position of utmost honor — how can it be broadly applied to ministers below!"
translations.idiomatic: But 'Supreme' denotes the summit of honor — it cannot be handed out to subjects below!"

sentences.zh: 廷尉少卿袁翻曰：「周官：上公九命，上大夫四命。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Fan said: "The Offices of Zhou: grand duke nine commands, senior grandee four commands.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Fan of the Court of Judicial Review said: "The Rites of Zhou set nine commands for a grand duke and four for a senior grandee.

sentences.zh: 命數雖殊，同為上，何必上者皆是極尊？」

translations.literal: Though the command numbers differ, both are "supreme" — why must every "supreme" be utmost honor?"
translations.idiomatic: The numbers differ, yet both use 'supreme' — not every 'supreme' need mean the highest dignity."

sentences.zh: 普惠厲聲訶翻曰：「禮有下卿上士，[4]何止大夫與公！

translations.literal: Puhui in a harsh voice rebuked Fan: "The rites have lower grandee above senior serviceman — [4] not only grandee and duke!
translations.idiomatic: Puhui raised his voice and rebuked Fan: "The rites speak of a lower grandee ranking above a senior serviceman — [4] the word 'supreme' applies far beyond grandee and duke!

sentences.zh: 但今所行，以太加上，二名雙舉，不得非極。

translations.literal: But what is now enacted uses Supreme joined with Duke, both names doubled together — it cannot but be utmost.
translations.idiomatic: What is proposed pairs 'Supreme' with 'Duke' — two superlatives at once. That can only mean the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 雕蟲小藝，微或相許，至於此處，豈卿所及！」

translations.literal: Petty ornamental skills — one might slightly concede — but on this point, is it within your reach!"
translations.idiomatic: Trifling scholarly quibbles I might indulge — but on a matter of this weight, it is beyond your ken!"

sentences.zh: 翻甚有慚色， 默不復言。

translations.literal: Fan was deeply ashamed in countenance, and silently spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Fan flushed with shame and said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄曰：「諫諍之體，各言所見，至於用捨，固在應時。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng said: "The substance of remonstrance and correction is that each states what he sees; as for adoption or rejection, that indeed rests on what suits the times.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng said: "Remonstrance means each man speaks his mind; whether advice is taken turns on the moment.

sentences.zh: 卿向答袁氏，聲何太厲？」

translations.literal: When you just now answered the Yuan clan, why was your voice so harsh?"
translations.idiomatic: Why did you answer Master Yuan in so fierce a tone just now?"

sentences.zh: 普惠對曰：「所言若是，宜見採用；

translations.literal: Puhui replied: "If what is said is correct, it ought to be adopted;
translations.idiomatic: Puhui replied: "If a point is sound, it should be heeded;

sentences.zh: 所言若非，懼有罪及。

translations.literal: If what is said is not correct, one fears guilt will reach.
translations.idiomatic: if it is unsound, I fear the kingdom will suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 是非須辨，非為苟競。」

translations.literal: Right and wrong must be distinguished — this is not for frivolous contention."
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong must be settled — I was not quarreling for sport."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「朝廷方開不諱之門，以廣忠言之路。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "The court has just opened a gate of no taboo, to broaden the path of loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said: "The court has only just opened its doors to frank speech, widening the way for loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 卿今意在向義，何云乃慮罪罰。」

translations.literal: Your intent now aims toward righteousness — why speak instead of fearing punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: Your heart is set on what is right — why speak as though you dread punishment?"

sentences.zh: 議者咸以太后當朝，志相崇順，遂奏曰：「張普惠辭雖不屈，然非臣等所同。

translations.literal: The discussants all, because the Empress Dowager held court and their wills inclined toward deferential compliance, thereupon submitted: "Zhang Puhui's words, though he did not yield, are yet not what we ministers agree with.
translations.idiomatic: The council, knowing the Empress Dowager reigned and eager to align with her wishes, reported: "Zhang Puhui has not yielded in argument, but we cannot join him.

sentences.zh: 渙汗已流，請依前詔。」

translations.literal: Sweat already flows — please follow the prior edict."
translations.idiomatic: The decree has already been issued — let it stand as before."

sentences.zh: 太后復遣元叉、賈璨宣令謂普惠曰：「朕向召卿與羣臣對議，往復既終，皆不同卿表。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager again sent Yuan Cha and Jia Can to announce the order, saying to Puhui: "We just now summoned you to debate with the ministers; the exchange is finished, and all differ from your memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sent Yuan Cha and Jia Can with a message for Puhui: "We called you to debate the ministers. The exchange is over, and none side with your petition.

sentences.zh: 朕之所行，孝子之志；

translations.literal: What We enact is a filial son's intent;
translations.idiomatic: What I do follows a filial son's duty;

sentences.zh: 卿之所陳，忠臣之道。

translations.literal: What you presented is a loyal minister's way.
translations.idiomatic: what you urged follows a loyal minister's path.

sentences.zh: 羣公已有成議，卿不得苦奪朕懷。

translations.literal: The assembled lords already have a settled decision — you must not bitterly wrest Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: The lords have decided. Do not try to wrench my resolve.

sentences.zh: 後有所見，勿得難言。」

translations.literal: Hereafter, if you have views, do not fail to speak hard words.
translations.idiomatic: When you have further views, speak plainly — do not hold back.

sentences.zh: 普惠於是拜令辭還。

translations.literal: Puhui thereupon bowed to the order and withdrew with farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui bowed, accepted the command, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，普惠被召，傳詔馳驊騮馬來，甚迅速，佇立催去，普惠諸子憂怖涕泣。

translations.literal: Initially, when Puhui was summoned, the edict-bearer came galloping on a sorrel horse, very swiftly; standing waiting, he urged departure — Puhui's sons were worried and fearful, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Puhui was summoned, a messenger spurred a sorrel stallion to the door and pressed him to leave at once. His sons wept in terror.

sentences.zh: 普惠謂曰：「我當休明之朝，掌諫議之職，若不言所難言，諫所難諫，便是唯唯，曠官尸祿。

translations.literal: Puhui said to them: "I serve in a flourishing and enlightened court, holding the office of Remonstrance Counselor — if I do not speak what is hard to speak, remonstrate where remonstrance is hard, then I am merely assenting, holding office in vain and consuming salary.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui told them: "In this bright age I hold the remonstrance. If I will not speak the unspeakable and warn where warning is hard, I am a yes-man — a deadweight on the payroll.

sentences.zh: 人生有死，死得其所，夫復何恨。

translations.literal: Human life has death — if one dies in the right place, what more regret is there.
translations.idiomatic: All men die. To die in the right cause — what regret could there be?

sentences.zh: 然朝廷有道，汝輩勿憂。」

translations.literal: Yet the court has the Way — you all, do not worry.
translations.idiomatic: And this court holds to the Way. Have no fear.

sentences.zh: 及議罷，旨勞還宅，親故賀其幸甚。

translations.literal: When the debate ended, an edict of gracious concern sent him home; kin and friends congratulated him on his great fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When the debate ended, an imperial message of reassurance sent him home. Relatives and friends hailed his deliverance.

sentences.zh: 時中山莊弼遺書普惠曰：[5]「明侯淵儒碩學，身負大才，秉此公方，來居諫職，謇謇如也，諤諤如也。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongshan Zhuang Bi sent Puhui a letter saying: [5] "Illustrious Marquis — a profound Confucian scholar of vast learning, personally bearing great talent, holding this upright fairness, come to occupy the remonstrance office — upright, upright; honest, honest.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhongshan Zhuang Bi wrote Puhui: [5] "Your Excellency — a scholar of depth and stature, great talent and public rectitude in the remonstrator's chair, steadfast and outspoken alike.

sentences.zh: 一昨承胡司徒第，當面折庭諍，雖問難鋒至，而應對響出，宋城之帶始縈，魯門之柝裁警，終使羣后逡巡，庶僚拱默，雖不見用於一時，固已傳美於百代。

translations.literal: The other day at Vice Minister Hu's residence, you spoke bluntly in open court debate; though probing questions came sharp as spear-points, your replies rang forth — as when Song of Cheng's belt was first girded, as when Lu's gate watchman's clapper was just sounded — in the end you made the lords hesitant and the officials bow in silence; though not employed for the moment, already your fame will pass through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday at Vice Minister Hu's house you disputed face to face in open court. Questions flew like spear-points; your answers rang clear as bells — the belt of Song of Cheng newly girded, the watchman's clapper at Lu's gate just struck — until the lords wavered and the officials stood mute. Though the court did not heed you today, your name will shine for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 聞風快然，敬裁此白。」

translations.literal: Hearing of this I am gladly stirred; respectfully I compose this note.
translations.idiomatic: Your courage lifts my heart. I write this in admiration.

sentences.zh: 普惠美其此書，每為口實。

translations.literal: Puhui praised this letter of his and often made it material for conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui treasured the letter and retold its lines often.

sentences.zh: 普惠以天下民調，幅度長廣，尚書計奏，復徵綿麻，恐其勞民不堪命，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Puhui, because the empire's common people's tax quotas had broad dimensions and length, and the Minister of the Household in calculating memorialized to levy hemp and flax again, fearing it would burden the people beyond what they could bear, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Puhui saw that tax quotas nationwide had swelled in measure, weight, and length, and that the Ministry of Revenue had petitioned to restore the hemp-and-flax levy. Fearing the people would be crushed, he memorialized the throne:

sentences.zh: 伏聞尚書奏復綿麻之調，尊先皇之軌，夙宵惟度，忻戰交集。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in hearing that the Minister of the Household memorializes restoring the hemp-and-flax quota, honoring the Former Emperor's standard — from dawn to night considering it, joy and trepidation interweave.
translations.idiomatic: I have learned that the Ministry memorializes to restore the hemp-and-flax levy, honoring my late father's standard. Day and night I weigh this — my joy and my dread come at once.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 聞復高祖舊典，所以忻惟新；

translations.literal: Hearing the restoration of Emperor Gaozu's old canon — therefore I rejoice at renewal;
translations.idiomatic: To hear Gaozu's old measure restored fills me with hope for renewal;

sentences.zh: 俱可復而不復，所以戰違法。

translations.literal: what all could be restored yet is not restored — therefore I tremble at violating law.
translations.idiomatic: yet what could all be restored is not — and that terrifies me as a breach of law.

sentences.zh: 仰惟高祖廢大斗，去長尺，改重秤，所以愛萬姓，從薄賦。

translations.literal: Looking up to consider Emperor Gaozu abolished the large peck, removed the long foot, changed the heavy steelyard — thereby to love the myriad people and follow light levies.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu abolished oversized pecks, shortened the foot, lightened the steelyard — all to spare the people and keep taxes lean.

sentences.zh: 知軍國須綿麻之用，故云幅度之間，億兆應有綿麻之利，故絹上稅綿八兩，布上稅麻十五斤。

translations.literal: Knowing army and state required hemp and flax use, therefore he said among dimensions, the hundred million ought to have hemp-and-flax benefit — therefore on silk he taxed eight ounces of floss, on cloth fifteen pounds of hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the army and state still needed hemp and flax, he held that within proper measures the realm could spare it — eight ounces of floss per bolt of silk, fifteen pounds of hemp per bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 萬姓得廢大斗，去長尺，改重秤，荷輕賦之饒，不適於綿麻而已，[6]故歌舞以供其賦，奔走以役其勤，天子信於上，億兆樂於下。

translations.literal: The myriad people obtained abolition of the large peck, removal of the long foot, change of the heavy steelyard, and bore the bounty of light levies — not only in hemp and flax alone, [6] therefore they sang and danced to supply their levies, ran to serve their toil; the Son of Heaven had trust above, the hundred million rejoiced below.
translations.idiomatic: The people gained lighter pecks, shorter feet, and lighter steelyards, and enjoyed leaner taxes — not only on hemp and flax, [6] so they sang as they paid and hurried to their labor; the Son of Heaven stood trusted above, and the masses rejoiced below.

sentences.zh: 故易曰：悅以使民，民忘其勞。

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes says: Delight to employ the people, and the people forget their toil.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Book of Changes: "Win the people with joy, and they forget their fatigue."

sentences.zh: 此之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the meaning.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，漸漸長闊，百姓嗟怨，聞於朝野。

translations.literal: From this downward, gradually broad and wide — the hundred people's sighs and resentments are heard in court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the quotas have grown ever wider. The people's groans reach court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太后未臨朝之前，陛下居諒闇之日，宰輔不尋其本，知天下之怨綿麻，不察其輻廣、度長、秤重、斗大，革其所弊，存其可存，而特放綿麻之調，以悅天下之心，此所謂悅之不以道，愚臣所以未悅者也。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in considering that before the Empress Dowager held court, when Your Majesty dwelt in mourning seclusion, the chief ministers did not seek the root — knowing the empire's resentment over hemp and flax, yet not examining whether the wheel-spokes were broad, the foot long, the steelyard heavy, the peck large; reforming what was flawed, preserving what could be preserved, they singled out only abolishing the hemp-and-flax quota to please the empire's hearts — this is what is called delighting without the Way; therefore your foolish servant has not been delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Empress Dowager assumed the regency, while Your Majesty was in mourning, the chief ministers never addressed the root of the problem. They knew the realm resented the hemp-and-flax levy, yet never examined swollen measures, long feet, heavy steelyards, and oversized pecks. They kept the abuses and lifted only the hemp-and-flax tax to win hearts — delight without principle. That is why I cannot rejoice.

sentences.zh: 尚書既知國少綿麻，不惟法度之□易，[7]民言之可畏，便欲去天下之大信，棄已行之成詔，追前之非，遂後之失，奏求還復綿麻，以充國用。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Household, already knowing the state lacks hemp and flax, not only that legal standards are □ to alter, [7] and that the people's words are to be feared, then wished to remove the empire's great trust, abandon the established enacted edict, pursue the former fault, follow the latter error, and memorialized seeking to restore hemp and flax to fill state use.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry, knowing stores of hemp and flax run low, ignored how hard it is to change the law, [7] ignored how dangerous popular outrage can be, and now seeks to break the empire's trust, revoke a settled edict, undo a past mistake by repeating it, and restore the hemp-and-flax levy to fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 不思庫中大有綿麻，而羣官共竊之。

translations.literal: They did not consider that the storehouses hold much hemp and flax, while the assembled officials together steal it.
translations.idiomatic: They never reckoned that the granaries hold ample hemp and flax — while officials steal it among themselves.

sentences.zh: 愚臣以為於理未盡。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant considers that in principle this is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that this reasoning is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 今宮人請調度，[8]造衣物，必度忖秤量。

translations.literal: Now when palace personnel request quota allotments, [8] to make garments, they must measure by standard and weigh on the steelyard.
translations.idiomatic: When palace staff requisition cloth, [8] every garment is cut to official measure and weighed on the steelyard.

sentences.zh: 絹布，匹有尺丈之盈，一猶不計其廣；

translations.literal: For silk cloth, if a bolt has surplus in feet and inches of width, not one is counted toward the excess;
translations.idiomatic: If a bolt of silk runs wide by inches, no one counts the surplus;

sentences.zh: 絲綿，斤兼百銖之剩，未聞依律罪州郡。

translations.literal: for floss and hemp, if a pound carries a hundred zhu extra, one never hears of punishing the prefectures by law.
translations.idiomatic: if a pound of floss or hemp weighs a hundred zhu heavy, no one punishes the prefectures by statute.

sentences.zh: 若一匹之濫，一斤之惡，則鞭戶主，連三長，此所以教民以貪者也。

translations.literal: Yet if one bolt is excessive or one pound is inferior, then the household head is flogged and the three chiefs are implicated — this is what teaches the people greed.
translations.idiomatic: But let one bolt be short or one pound be shoddy, and the household head is flogged while the local chiefs are punished — thus the state teaches the people to cheat.

sentences.zh: 今百官請俸，人樂長闊，并欲厚重，無復準極。

translations.literal: Now when the hundred officials request salaries, each delights in broad dimensions and heavy thickness, all wishing for weight and bulk, with no standard limit any longer.
translations.idiomatic: Officials drawing salaries now all prefer bolts that are wide, thick, and heavy — with no fixed standard left.

sentences.zh: 得長闊厚重者，便云其州能調，絹布精闊且長，橫發美譽，以亂視聽；

translations.literal: Whoever obtains broad, thick, and heavy goods then says that prefecture can levy well — silk and cloth fine, broad, and long — and recklessly sends up glowing praise to confuse sight and hearing;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever gets the widest, thickest bolts declares his prefecture an expert levier — fine silk, broad and long — and floods the court with praise to dazzle the eye and ear;

sentences.zh: 不聞嫌長惡廣，求計還官者。

translations.literal: one never hears of disliking length or hating breadth, seeking to calculate and return to the office.
translations.idiomatic: yet no one is ever heard complaining of excess length or width and returning the surplus to the state.

sentences.zh: 此百司所以仰負聖明也。

translations.literal: This is why the hundred offices rely on and burden the sage clarity.
translations.idiomatic: That is why every office lives off Your Majesty's forbearance.

sentences.zh: 今若必復綿麻者，謂宜先令四海知其所由，明立嚴禁，復本幅度，新綿麻之典，依太和之稅。

translations.literal: If hemp and flax must now be restored, I say one should first make the four seas know the reason, clearly establish strict prohibitions, restore the original dimensions, and make the new hemp-and-flax canon follow the Taihe-era levy.
translations.idiomatic: If the hemp-and-flax levy must return, let the realm first know why: set strict rules, restore the original measures, and model the new levy on the Taihe standard.

sentences.zh: 其在庫絹布并及絲綿，不依典制者，請遣一尚書與太府卿、左右藏令，依今官度、官秤，計其斤兩、廣長，折給請俸之人。

translations.literal: As for silk cloth and floss and hemp in the storehouses that do not follow the canonical standard, please send one Minister of the Household with the Grand Storehouse Director and the Left and Right Storehouse Directors, using present official measure and official steelyard, to calculate their pounds and ounces, breadth and length, and convert payment to those requesting salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Silk, cloth, floss, and hemp in the storehouses that fall short of the standard should be measured by a Minister of the Household, the Grand Storehouse Director, and the Left and Right Storehouse Directors with official rule and steelyard — weighed, measured, and paid out to salary claimants in kind.

sentences.zh: 總常俸之數，千俸所出，以布綿麻，亦應其一歲之用。

translations.literal: Totalling the number of regular salaries — of what a thousand salaries issue, in cloth, floss, and hemp, there ought likewise to be enough for one year's use.
translations.idiomatic: Count the regular salaries: what a thousand stipends require in cloth, floss, and hemp should cover a full year's need.

sentences.zh: [9]使天下知二聖之心，愛民惜法如此，則高祖之軌中興於神龜，明明慈信照布於無窮，則孰不幸甚。

translations.literal: [9] Let the empire know the hearts of the Two Sages — loving the people and cherishing law thus — then Emperor Gaozu's standard will be revived in the Shengui era, bright benevolence and trust shining boundlessly; who then would not count himself most fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Let the realm see that the Two Sages love the people and honor the law — then Gaozu's standard will rise again in the Shengui reign, bright mercy and trust shining without end, and who would not call himself blessed?

sentences.zh: 伏願亮臣悾悾之至，下慰蒼生之心。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in wishing you to illumine my utmost sincerity, below to comfort the dark masses' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh my earnest plea and ease the hearts of the people below.

sentences.zh: 普惠又表乞朝直之日，時聽奉見。

translations.literal: Puhui again memorialized, requesting that on days of court attendance he be allowed to present himself at audience from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui also petitioned to be received in audience on his regular court days.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，月一陛見。

translations.literal: From this onward, once a month he ascended to audience.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was granted an audience once a month.

sentences.zh: 又以肅宗不親視朝，過崇佛法，郊廟之事，多委有司，上疏曰：「臣聞明德卹祀，成湯光六百之祚；

translations.literal: Also, because Emperor Suzong did not personally view court, excessively honored Buddhist Law, and for suburban and temple affairs mostly delegated to the responsible offices, he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the enlightened virtue cares for sacrifice — Cheng Tang brightened six hundred years of fortune;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Emperor Suzong no longer held court in person, lavished favor on Buddhism, and left suburban rites and temple affairs mostly to subordinates, he memorialized: "I have read that enlightened virtue nourishes sacrifice — Cheng Tang secured six centuries of rule;

sentences.zh: 嚴父配天，孔子稱周公其人也。

translations.literal: honoring the father and matching Heaven — Confucius said the Duke of Zhou was such a man.
translations.idiomatic: honoring one's father as Heaven's peer — Confucius said the Duke of Zhou was such a man.

sentences.zh: 故能馨香上聞，福傳遐世。

translations.literal: Therefore fragrance rises above to be heard, and blessing passes to distant ages.
translations.idiomatic: Thus offerings rise to Heaven, and blessings reach far generations.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下重暉纂統，欽明文思，天地屬心，百神佇望，故宜敦崇祀禮，咸秩無文。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in considering that Your Majesty, inheriting doubled radiance and continuing the succession, reverently illumined and literarily thoughtful — Heaven and Earth turn their hearts to you, the hundred spirits await in hope — therefore you ought to thickly honor sacrificial rites, all in due order without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits a doubled radiance and a weighty mandate; Heaven and Earth look to you, the hundred spirits await — you should therefore exalt every rite in its proper season, omitting none.

sentences.zh: 而告朔朝廟，不親於明堂；

translations.literal: Yet announcing the first of the month and attending the ancestral temple — not in person at the Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the monthly temple announcements — You do not perform them in person at the Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 嘗禘郊社，多委於有司。

translations.literal: seasonal offerings at the suburban altars and state altars — mostly delegated to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: seasonal suburban and state sacrifices — mostly left to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 觀射遊苑，躍馬騁中，危而非典，豈清蹕之意。

translations.literal: Viewing archery, roaming the parks, leaping horses and galloping at heart — perilous and not canonical — how is this the intent of clearing the road?
translations.idiomatic: Watching archery, roaming the parks, spurring horses in reckless sport — dangerous and unbefitting — is this what clearing the imperial path means?

sentences.zh: 殖不思之冥業，損巨費於生民。

translations.literal: Amassing heedless netherworld undertakings, squandering vast expense on the living people.
translations.idiomatic: Heaping up thoughtless merit for the afterlife while draining the living.

sentences.zh: 減祿削力，近供無事之僧；

translations.literal: Reducing salaries and cutting labor, near at hand supplying idle monks;
translations.idiomatic: Salaries are cut and labor withheld to feed idle monks nearby;

sentences.zh: 崇飾雲殿，遠邀未然之報。

translations.literal: grandly adorning cloud halls, far off inviting rewards not yet come.
translations.idiomatic: cloud halls are lavishly gilded to buy blessings not yet earned.

sentences.zh: 昧爽之臣，稽首於外；

translations.literal: Ministers at dawn bow their heads outside;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn ministers kowtow in the outer court;

sentences.zh: 玄寂之眾，遨遊於內。

translations.literal: the darkly silent multitude roam within.
translations.idiomatic: while silent monks wander inside.

sentences.zh: 愆禮忤時，人靈未穆。

translations.literal: Transgressing rites and going against the times — the human spirits are not yet tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Rites are breached and the age is unsettled — spirits and men alike are disturbed.

sentences.zh: 愚謂從朝夕之因，[10]求秖劫之果，未若先萬國之忻心，以事其親，使天下和平，災害不生者也。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant considers that from causes of morning and evening, [10] seeking the fruit of a kalpa, is not equal to first winning the myriad states' rejoicing hearts to serve one's parents — making the empire peaceful and disasters not arising.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that chasing kalpa-long rewards through daily devotions [10] cannot match winning the joy of the realm and serving one's parents — bringing peace under Heaven and warding off disaster.

sentences.zh: 伏願淑慎威儀，萬邦作式，躬致郊廟之虔，親紆朔望之禮，釋奠成均，竭心千畝，明發不寐，潔誠禋祼。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in wishing you would be good, cautious, and majestic in bearing — a model for the myriad states; personally perform suburban and temple devotion; personally conduct the first-of-month and new-moon rites; libation at the Completed Harmony Academy; exhaust your heart on the thousand-mu field; rise at dawn without sleep; pure sincerity in border and libation rites.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to guard your dignity as a model to all lands: attend the suburban altars yourself, perform the monthly and new-moon rites, offer at the Imperial Academy, labor at the sacred field, rise before dawn, and pour your heart into every sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 孝悌可以通神明，德教可以光四海，則一人有喜，兆民賴之。

translations.literal: Filial piety and brotherliness can reach the spirits; virtue and teaching can illumine the four seas — then when one man has joy, the myriad people rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety can reach the spirits; moral teaching can light the four seas — when the ruler rejoices, the masses prosper with him.

sentences.zh: 然後精進三寶，信心如來。

translations.literal: Only then advance the Three Treasures, with faith like the Thus-Come One.
translations.idiomatic: Only then advance the Three Treasures and trust in the Buddha as he deserves.

sentences.zh: 道由禮深，故諸漏可盡；

translations.literal: The Way follows from rites deeply rooted — therefore all outflows can be exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: When the Way grows from deep roots in rites, every defilement can be drained;

sentences.zh: 法隨禮積，故彼岸可登。

translations.literal: the Law follows as rites accumulate — therefore the farther shore can be reached.
translations.idiomatic: when the Law builds on accumulated rites, the farther shore can be reached.

sentences.zh: 量撤僧寺不急之華，還復百官久折之秩。

translations.literal: Measure withdrawal of non-urgent ornament from Buddhist temples, and restore the long-reduced ranks of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Trim needless splendor from the temples and restore the salaries long withheld from officials.

sentences.zh: 已興之構，務從簡成；

translations.literal: Structures already raised — see that they are completed simply;
translations.idiomatic: What is already under construction should be finished plainly;

sentences.zh: 將來之造，權令停息。

translations.literal: works yet to come — for the time being command them to cease.
translations.idiomatic: what is not yet begun should be halted for now.

sentences.zh: 仍舊亦可，何必改作。

translations.literal: Keeping the old can also suffice — why must one change and rebuild?
translations.idiomatic: The old ways would suffice — why rebuild at all?

sentences.zh: 庶節用愛人，法俗俱賴。

translations.literal: Perhaps then economy in use and love for people — law and custom both will rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Then thrift and care for the people would benefit both law and custom alike.

sentences.zh: 臣學不經遠，言多孟浪，忝職其憂，不敢默爾。」

translations.literal: Your servant's learning does not reach far; my words are mostly rash — holding office with this worry, I dare not be silent.
translations.idiomatic: My learning is shallow and my words rash, but holding this office I dare not stay silent.

sentences.zh: 尋別敕付外，議釋奠之禮。

translations.literal: Soon afterward a separate edict was issued to the outer court to discuss the libation rite at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict went out to the outer court to debate the Imperial Academy libation rite.

sentences.zh: 時史官剋日蝕，豫敕罷朝。

translations.literal: At the time the historiographers fixed a date for an eclipse and preemptively ordered court dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The court astronomers predicted an eclipse and preemptively canceled audience.

sentences.zh: 普惠以逆廢非禮，上疏陳之。

translations.literal: Puhui, because preemptive dismissal was not according to rites, submitted a memorial stating this.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui held that canceling court in advance violated ritual and memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 又表論時政得失。

translations.literal: He also memorialized discussing the gains and losses of current government.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial on the strengths and failings of current policy.

sentences.zh: 一曰，審法度，平斗尺，租調務輕，賦役務省。

translations.literal: First: examine laws and standards, level bushels and measures; land tax and corvée dues should aim to be light, labor levies should aim to be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: First, enforce fair laws and uniform measures, keep land taxes light, and reduce labor levies wherever possible.

sentences.zh: 二曰，聽輿言，察怨訟，先皇舊事有不便於政者，請悉追改。

translations.literal: Second: listen to voices from the carts, examine grievances and lawsuits; where the former emperor's old precedents are inconvenient for government, I ask that all be traced back and revised.
translations.idiomatic: Second, heed public opinion and investigate complaints; any precedent from the late emperor that harms governance should be reviewed and corrected.

sentences.zh: 三曰，進忠謇，退不肖，任賢勿貳，去邪勿疑。

translations.literal: Third: advance the loyal and forthright, dismiss the unworthy; employ the worthy without duplicity, remove the wicked without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Third, promote the loyal and remove the unfit; trust the worthy completely and purge the corrupt without wavering.

sentences.zh: 四曰，興滅國，繼絕世，勳親之胤，所宜收敍。

translations.literal: Fourth: raise up extinguished states, continue severed lineages; descendants of meritorious kin ought to be gathered and restored.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, revive fallen houses and restore broken lines — especially the descendants of honored imperial kin, who deserve reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 書奏，肅宗、靈太后引普惠於宣光殿，隨事難詰，延對移時。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Suzong and Empress Dowager Ling summoned Puhui to Xuanguang Hall, challenging him item by item, and the audience lasted a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was in, Emperor Suzong and Empress Dowager Ling brought Puhui to Xuanguang Hall and pressed him on each point until the session ran long.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「寧有先皇之詔，一一翻改！」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Can there be former emperor's edicts, overturned one by one!
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Would you overturn every edict of the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 普惠僶俛不言。

translations.literal: Puhui bowed low and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui bowed his head and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「卿似欲致諫，故以左右有人，不肯苦言。

translations.literal: An edict said: "You seem to wish to offer remonstrance, yet because attendants are present, you are unwilling to speak frankly.
translations.idiomatic: The edict continued: "You wish to remonstrate, I think, but with others watching you hold back.

sentences.zh: 朕為卿屏左右，卿其盡陳之。」

translations.literal: I will screen the attendants away for you — speak your fill."
translations.idiomatic: I shall dismiss everyone — say whatever you mean to say."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聖人之養庶物，愛之如傷，況今二聖纂承洪緒，妻承夫，子承父，夫、父之不可，安然仍行，豈先帝傳委之本意？

translations.literal: He replied: "The sage nourishes the myriad things, loving them as if wounded; how much more now, when the Two Sages succeed the great enterprise — wife succeeding husband, son succeeding father — what husband and father could not tolerate is still carried on as if nothing were wrong; how can this be the original intent of the late emperor's transmission of mandate?
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "The sage nurtures all living things as if each wound pained him. Now the Two Sages inherit a vast enterprise — as wife succeeds husband and son succeeds father — policies a husband and father would never have tolerated continue unchanged. Is this what the late emperor intended when he entrusted you with the realm?

sentences.zh: 仰惟先帝行事，或有司之謬，或權時所行，在後以為不可者，皆追而正之。

translations.literal: Looking up to consider the late emperor's acts, whether errors of officials or measures taken from expediency — what later was deemed wrong has all been traced back and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Under the late emperor, whether through official error or temporary expedient, anything later judged wrong was revisited and set right.

sentences.zh: 聖上忘先帝之自新，不問理之伸屈，一皆抑之，豈蒼生黎庶所仰望於聖德？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty forgets the late emperor's self-renewal, does not ask whether right is extended or bent, and suppresses all alike — how can this be what the black-haired masses hope for in sagely virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has forgotten that the late emperor reformed himself, does not weigh the merits of each grievance, and rejects them all — is this what the people expect of sagely rule?

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「小小細務，一一翻動，更成煩擾。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Petty little matters, overturned one by one, would only create further bother."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "Fussing over every petty detail would only breed more disorder."

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「聖上之養庶物，若慈母之養赤子。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "Your Majesty's nourishing of the myriad things is like a loving mother nourishing her infant.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui said: "Your Majesty cares for the people as a loving mother cares for her infant.

sentences.zh: 今赤子幾臨危壑，將赴水火，以煩勞而不救，豈赤子所望於慈母！」

translations.literal: Now the infant nearly faces a perilous ravine, about to plunge into fire and water — and because of bother you do not save; how can this be what an infant hopes for from a loving mother!
translations.idiomatic: That infant now teeters over a chasm, about to fall into fire — if the mother refuses rescue because it is inconvenient, what infant would call her loving?

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「天下蒼生，寧有如此苦事？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Under Heaven's black-haired masses, could there truly be such suffering?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "Surely the people of the realm do not suffer so terribly?"

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「天下之親懿，莫重於太師彭城王，然遂不免枉死。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "Among all kin of honored virtue under Heaven, none was weightier than Grand Preceptor Prince of Pengcheng, yet he still could not escape unjust death.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui said: "Of all imperial kin, none was closer than the Prince of Pengcheng, Grand Preceptor — yet even he died unjustly.

sentences.zh: 微細之苦，何可得無？」

translations.literal: Fine, subtle suffering — how can it be absent?
translations.idiomatic: Can lesser wrongs not exist as well?

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「彭城之苦，吾已封其三子，何足復言！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Prince of Pengcheng's suffering — I have already enfeoffed his three sons; why bring it up again!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "I have already enfeoffed Pengcheng's three sons — there is nothing more to say!"

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「聖后封彭城之三子，天下莫不忻至德，知慈母之在上。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "The Holy Empress enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng's three sons — under Heaven none failed to rejoice at supreme virtue, knowing a loving mother is above.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui said: "When Your Majesty enfeoffed Pengcheng's three sons, the realm rejoiced at your supreme virtue and knew a loving mother sat above them.

sentences.zh: 臣所以重陳者，凡如此枉，乞垂聖察。」

translations.literal: Your servant's reason for repeating himself is: every injustice such as this, I beg you to bestow sagely scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: I repeat myself only because I ask Your Majesty to examine every such wrong.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿云『興滅國，繼絕世』，滅國絕世，竟復誰是？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "You say 'raise extinguished states, continue severed lineages' — extinguished states and severed lineages, in the end who are they?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "You speak of raising fallen states and continuing broken lines — who exactly do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 普惠曰：「昔淮南逆終，漢文封其四子，蓋骨肉之不可棄，親親故也。

translations.literal: Puhui said: "Formerly when Huainan's rebellion ended, Emperor Wen of Han enfeoffed his four sons — this is because bone and flesh may not be abandoned; close kin to close kin, therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui answered: "When the Prince of Huainan's revolt ended, Emperor Wen enfeoffed his four sons — flesh and blood must not be cast aside; such is the principle of honoring kin.

sentences.zh: 竊見故太尉咸陽王、冀州刺史京兆王，乃皇子皇孫，一德之虧，自貽悔戾，沉淪幽壤，緬焉弗收，豈是興滅繼絕之意？

translations.literal: I privately observe the late Grand Commandant Prince of Xianyang and Jizhou Inspector Prince of Jingzhao — they were imperial sons and grandsons; one fault in virtue, they brought regret and rebellion on themselves, sank into the dark earth, and were removed far away without recovery — how is this the intent of raising the extinguished and continuing the severed?
translations.idiomatic: I note that the late Prince of Xianyang, Grand Commandant, and the Prince of Jingzhao, Jizhou inspector — both imperial sons and grandsons — lost their way and brought ruin on themselves, yet lie unburied in dark graves, forgotten without recall. Is this what it means to raise the fallen and restore broken lines?

sentences.zh: 乞收葬二王，封其子孫，愚臣之願。」

translations.literal: I beg to gather and bury the two princes, enfeoff their descendants — this foolish servant's wish.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the two princes be gathered and buried and their descendants enfeoffed — this is my humble plea.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿言有理，朕深戢之，當命公卿博議此事。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Your words have reason; I deeply acknowledge them and shall command the dukes and ministers to deliberate broadly on this matter."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "You make sense. I take your point to heart and will have the high ministers debate the matter."

sentences.zh: 及任城王澄薨，普惠以吏民之義，又荷其恩待，朔望奔赴，至於禫除，雖寒暑風雨，無不必至。

translations.literal: When Prince of Rencheng Chen died, Puhui out of the obligation of officials and people, and also bearing his grace and regard, on each new and full moon rushed to attend, until the end of mourning; though cold, heat, wind, or rain, he never failed to come.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Rencheng Chen died, Puhui — bound by duty and deep in his debt — attended every new and full moon through the full mourning period, never missing a visit regardless of weather.

sentences.zh: 初澄嘉賞普惠，臨薨，啟為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Initially Chen greatly valued Puhui; on the verge of death he recommended him as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had long admired Puhui and on his deathbed recommended him for Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 靈太后既深悼澄，覽啟從之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, deeply mourning Chen, read the recommendation and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, grieving deeply for Chen, read the recommendation and assented.

sentences.zh: 詔行之後，尚書諸郎以普惠地寒，不應便居管轄，相與為約，並欲不復上省，紛紜多日乃息。

translations.literal: After the edict was promulgated, the various bureau chiefs of the Masters of Writing, because Puhui's background was humble, held that he should not immediately hold supervisory rank; they made a pact among themselves and all wished no longer to report to court — the uproar lasted many days before it subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict, the bureau chiefs protested that Puhui's humble origins disqualified him from a supervisory post; they conspired to boycott court and the uproar lasted days before subsiding.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，詔遣楊鈞送蠕蠕主阿那瓌還國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang, an edict dispatched Yang Jun to escort the Rouran lord Ana-kwei back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang year 2, an edict ordered Yang Jun to escort Ana-kwei, the Rouran khan, back to his realm.

sentences.zh: 普惠謂遣之將貽後患，上疏曰：「臣聞乾元以利貞為大，非義則不動；

translations.literal: Puhui held that sending him back would leave later troubles; he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the Creative's virtue takes firm benefit as greatest — without righteousness it does not act;
translations.idiomatic: Puhui warned that repatriating him would bring future disaster and memorialized: "I have heard that Heaven's virtue rests on steadfast benefit — it does not act without justice;

sentences.zh: 皇王以博施為功，非類則不從。

translations.literal: kings and emperors take broad bestowal as merit — what is not of their kind they do not follow.
translations.idiomatic: and that rulers achieve merit through generous governance — they do not embrace what is alien.

sentences.zh: 故能始萬物而化天下者也。

translations.literal: Thus they can originate the myriad things and transform all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus can they nurture all things and transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下叡哲欽明，道光虞舜，八表宅心，九服清晏。

translations.literal: Humbly considering, Your Majesty is wise, discerning, and reverently bright; your virtue matches Emperor Shun; the eight directions lodge their hearts in you; the nine domains are clear and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage and brilliant, your virtue rivaling Shun's; the far reaches of the realm look to you and all lands enjoy peace.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕相害於朔垂，妖師扇亂於江外，此乃封豕長蛇，不識王度，天將悔其罪，所以奉皇魏。

translations.literal: Rouran harm one another on the northern frontier; demonic teachers stir chaos beyond the Yangtze — these are bloated boar and long serpent, knowing not kingly standard; Heaven will repent their sins, therefore they submit to Imperial Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran fight among themselves on the northern marches while sorcerers foment disorder south of the Yangtze — bloated boars and great serpents who know no king's law; Heaven will soon punish their crimes, which is why they now submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 故荼毒之，辛苦之，令知至道之可樂也。

translations.literal: Therefore they are afflicted and toiled, to make them know that the utmost Way can bring joy.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven afflicts and toils them so they may learn the joy of the true Way.

sentences.zh: 宜安民以悅其志，恭己以懷其心。

translations.literal: One should settle the people to please their aspirations, and defer to others to embrace their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: You should ease your people to win their hearts and govern with humility to win theirs.

sentences.zh: 而先自勞擾，艱難下民，興師郊甸之內，遠投荒塞之外，救累世之勁敵，可謂無名之師。

translations.literal: Yet first you yourself toil and disturb, burdening the lower people; you raise armies within the suburban domain and cast them far beyond the wild passes, to rescue a fierce enemy of many generations — this can be called an army without name.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you first exhaust yourselves and burden the people — raising armies at home to march beyond the frontier wilderness and rescue a hereditary foe. This is an army without cause.

sentences.zh: 諺曰『唯亂門之無過』，愚情未見其可。

translations.literal: A proverb says 'only chaos at the gate has no excess' — this foolish sentiment does not see how it can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says only chaos at your own gate is trouble enough — I see no wisdom in this plan.

sentences.zh: 當是邊將窺竊一時之功，不思兵為凶器，不得已而用之者也。

translations.literal: This must be border generals coveting momentary merit, not thinking that arms are an instrument of ill omen, to be used only when there is no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: Border generals must be grasping for quick glory, forgetting that war is a weapon of last resort.

sentences.zh: 夫白登之役，漢祖親困之。

translations.literal: As for the campaign at Baideng, Emperor Gaozu of Han was personally trapped there.
translations.idiomatic: At Baideng, Emperor Gaozu of Han was himself besieged.

sentences.zh: 樊噲欲以十萬眾橫行匈奴中，季布以為不可，請斬之。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai wished with a hundred thousand troops to march freely through the Xiongnu; Ji Bu held it impossible and asked to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai proposed leading a hundred thousand men to sweep through the Xiongnu; Ji Bu called it folly and demanded his execution.

sentences.zh: 千載以為美。

translations.literal: A thousand years have taken this as beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: History has honored that judgment for a millennium.

sentences.zh: 況今旱酷異常，聖慈降膳，乃以萬五千人使楊鈞為將而欲定蠕蠕，忤時而動，其可濟乎？

translations.literal: How much more now, when drought is extraordinarily severe and sagely compassion has reduced court meals — yet with fifteen thousand men and Yang Jun as commander you wish to settle the Rouran; acting against the season, how can it succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Today drought is extraordinary and even the court has trimmed its meals — yet you send fifteen thousand men under Yang Jun to subdue the Rouran. Acting against the season, how can this succeed?

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌投命皇朝，撫之可也，豈容困疲我兆民以資天喪之虜。

translations.literal: Ana-kwei entrusted his life to the imperial court — comfort him and it suffices; how can you allow exhausting and wearing down our myriad people to aid barbarians Heaven marks for destruction?
translations.idiomatic: Ana-kwei has cast himself on the court's mercy — shelter him. How can you exhaust our people to succor enemies Heaven itself has condemned?

sentences.zh: 昔莊公納子糾，以致乾時之敗；

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Zhuang of Lu received Prince Jiu, thereby causing the defeat at Ganshi;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang of Lu once sheltered Prince Jiu and brought on the defeat at Ganshi;

sentences.zh: 魯僖以邾國，而有懸冑之耻。

translations.literal: Duke Xi of Lu relied on the state of Zhu and suffered the shame of helmets hung upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi of Lu leaned on Zhu and suffered the shame of inverted helmets.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕時亂，後主繼立，雖云散亡，姦虞難抑。

translations.literal: Now the Rouran are in timely chaos; a successor lord has newly risen; though they say they are scattered and lost, treachery and plotting are hard to suppress.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran are in turmoil and a new khan has risen; though they appear scattered, treachery is hard to suppress.

sentences.zh: 脫有井陘之慮，楊鈞之肉其可食乎！

translations.literal: If there should be concern like at Jingxing Pass, could Yang Jun's flesh be eaten!
translations.idiomatic: If disaster strikes as at Jingxing, what would become of Yang Jun and his men?

sentences.zh: 高車、蠕蠕，連兵積年，飢饉相仍，須其自斃，小亡大傷，然後一舉而并之。

translations.literal: Gaoche and Rouran have battled year after year, famine following famine; wait for them to destroy themselves — the smaller perishes, the larger is wounded — then in one stroke annex them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche and Rouran have warred for years amid endless famine; wait until they destroy each other — the weaker gone, the stronger crippled — then conquer both in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 此卞氏之高略，所以獲兩虎，不可不圖之。

translations.literal: This is Lady Bian's lofty strategy — therefore she obtained two tigers; it cannot but be planned.
translations.idiomatic: This is Lady Bian's stratagem of letting two tigers fight — it cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 今土山告難，簡書相續，蓋亦無能為也，正與今舉相會，天其或者欲以告戒人，不欲使南北兩疆，並興大眾。

translations.literal: Now Tushan reports difficulty, dispatches follow one after another — probably it too can do nothing; this exactly coincides with the present undertaking. Perhaps Heaven wishes to warn people, not wanting both northern and southern frontiers to raise great hosts at once.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan now sends urgent dispatches — it can barely cope — which coincides with this expedition. Perhaps Heaven warns us not to raise great armies on both frontiers at once.

sentences.zh: 脫狂狡構間於其間，而復事連中國，何以寧之？

translations.literal: If the cunning and fierce plot discord between them, and affairs again connect with China, how will you bring peace?
translations.idiomatic: If schemers sow discord between them and drag China into it, how will you restore peace?

sentences.zh: 今宰輔專欲好小名，不圖安危大計，此微臣所以寒心者也。

translations.literal: Now chief ministers exclusively wish to favor petty fame, not planning the great design of safety and peril — this is why this humble servant's heart grows cold.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers now chase petty glory and ignore the great question of security — that is why my heart grows cold.

sentences.zh: 那瓌之不還，負何信義？

translations.literal: If Ana-kwei does not return — what faith and righteousness would be violated?
translations.idiomatic: What breach of faith if Ana-kwei did not return?

sentences.zh: 此機之際，北師宜停。

translations.literal: At this juncture of opportunity, the northern army ought to halt.
translations.idiomatic: At this critical moment the northern expedition should be halted.

sentences.zh: 臣言不及義，文書所經過，不敢不陳。

translations.literal: Your servant's words may not reach righteousness, but as documents pass through my hands I dare not fail to state them.
translations.idiomatic: My words may fall short of wisdom, but as documents cross my desk I dare not stay silent.

sentences.zh: 兵猶火也，不戢將自焚。

translations.literal: Arms are like fire — if not restrained, they will burn oneself.
translations.idiomatic: War is like fire — unchecked, it consumes those who wield it.

sentences.zh: 二虜自滅之形，可以為殷鑒。

translations.literal: The form of the two barbarians' self-destruction can serve as a lesson from the past.
translations.idiomatic: The two barbarians' self-destruction is a lesson from history.

sentences.zh: 伏願輯和萬國，以靜四疆，混一之期，坐而自至矣。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish to harmonize the myriad states to settle the four frontiers; the time of unification will arrive without effort.
