translations.idiomatic: I pray you harmonize all lands and pacify the frontiers — unification will come without forcing it.

sentences.zh: 臣愚昧多違，必無可採，匹夫之智，願以呈獻。」

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and much at odds — surely nothing worth adopting; a common man's wisdom, offered for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: I am ignorant and often wrong; surely nothing here merits adoption — yet I offer this humble counsel.

sentences.zh: 表奏，詔答曰：「夫窮鳥歸人，尚或興惻，況那瓌嬰禍流離，遠來依庇，在情在國，何容弗矜。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict replied: "A bird in extremity returning to man still may stir compassion; how much more Ana-kwei, afflicted by disaster and wandering far, coming from afar to seek shelter — in feeling and in state, how can one fail to pity him?
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was answered: "A bird in distress returning to humans still stirs pity — how much more Ana-kwei, afflicted and exiled, coming from afar to seek refuge. In humanity and in statecraft alike, how can we show no compassion?

sentences.zh: 且納亡興喪，有國大義，皇魏堂堂，寧廢斯德。

translations.literal: Moreover, receiving the perishing and raising the fallen is a state's great righteousness; Imperial Wei is majestic — how can it abandon this virtue?
translations.idiomatic: To shelter the fallen and restore the ruined is a great duty of state — how can majestic Wei abandon such virtue?

sentences.zh: 後主亂亡，似當非謬，此送彼迎，想無拒戰。

translations.literal: The successor lord's disorder and ruin seems likely no error; we send him off and welcome the other — presumably no battle will be refused.
translations.idiomatic: The successor khan's collapse is real enough; escorting Ana-kwei home while welcoming him should meet no resistance.

sentences.zh: 國義宜表，朝算已決，卿深誠厚慮，朕用嘉戢。

translations.literal: State righteousness ought to be displayed; court strategy is decided; your deep sincerity and generous concern — I acknowledge them with approval.
translations.idiomatic: Our duty demands this display and the court's decision stands; your earnest concern I gratefully acknowledge.

sentences.zh: 但此段機略，不獲相從，脫後不逮，勿憚匡言。」

translations.literal: But on this segment of strategy I cannot follow you; if later it falls short, do not fear to offer corrective words."
translations.idiomatic: But on this strategy I cannot agree; if events prove me wrong, do not hesitate to speak again."

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍義州刺史文僧明舉城歸順，揚州刺史長孫稚遣別駕封壽入城固守，衍將裴邃、湛僧率眾攻逼，詔普惠為持節、東道行臺，攝軍司赴援之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yan's Yizhou Inspector Wen Sengming surrendered his city in submission; Yangzhou Inspector Zhangsun Zhi sent Vice Director Feng Shou into the city to hold firm; Yan's generals Pei Sui and Zhan Seng led troops to attack and press; an edict appointed Puhui as commissioner with credentials, Eastern Route Mobile Staff, acting army controller to go rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Sengming, Yizhou inspector under Xiao Yan, surrendered his city, Yangzhou inspector Zhangsun Zhi sent vice director Feng Shou to hold it. Yan's generals Pei Sui and Zhan Seng besieged them. Puhui was ordered as Eastern Route commissioner, acting army controller, to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 軍始渡淮，而封壽已棄城單馬而退。

translations.literal: The army had just crossed the Huai when Feng Shou had already abandoned the city and fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: The army had barely crossed the Huai when Feng Shou fled the city alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 軍罷還朝。

translations.literal: The army disbanded and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition ended and the army returned to court.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍弟子西豐侯正德詐稱降款，朝廷頗事當迎，普惠上疏，請赴揚州，移還蕭氏，不從。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's nephew Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde falsely claimed to surrender; the court largely considered welcoming him; Puhui submitted a memorial asking to go to Yangzhou and transfer him back to the Xiao clan — not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's nephew, Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde, feigned defection and the court nearly sent a welcome; Puhui memorialized to go to Yangzhou and send him back to the Xiao — overruled.

sentences.zh: 俄而，正德果逃還。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhengde indeed fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhengde fled back as predicted.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史石士基、行臺元洪超並贓貨被繩，以普惠為右將軍、涼州刺史，即為西行臺。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Inspector Shi Shiji and Mobile Staff Yuan Hongchao were both bound for bribery; Puhui was appointed General of the Right and Liangzhou Inspector, also serving as Western Route Mobile Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou inspector Shi Shiji and mobile staff chief Yuan Hongchao were prosecuted for bribery; Puhui was made General of the Right and Liangzhou inspector, concurrently Western Route commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以病辭免。

translations.literal: He declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He declined on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 除光祿大夫，右丞如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; right vice director as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, retaining his post as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 先是，仇池武興羣氐數反，西垂郡戍，租運久絕。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Di tribes of Chouci and Wuxing had repeatedly rebelled; western frontier garrison districts — grain transport had long ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Di of Chouci and Wuxing had rebelled repeatedly; grain shipments to western garrisons had long been cut off.

sentences.zh: 詔普惠以本官為持節、西道行臺。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Puhui in his existing office as commissioner with credentials, Western Route Mobile Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui was ordered in his existing rank as Western Route commissioner with full credentials.

sentences.zh: 給秦、岐、涇、華、雍、豳、東秦七州兵武三萬人，任其召發，送南秦、東益二州兵租，分付諸戍，其所部將統，聽於關西牧守之中隨機召遣，軍資板印之屬，悉以自隨。

translations.literal: He was given thirty thousand troops from Qin, Qi, Jing, Hua, Yong, Bin, and Eastern Qin prefectures, with authority to mobilize them; to deliver the military grain levies of Southern Qin and Eastern Yi prefectures and distribute them to the garrisons; the generals and commanders under his command were allowed to be summoned and dispatched at random from among the frontier governors of west of the passes; military supplies, seals, and the like — all to accompany him himself.
translations.idiomatic: He received thirty thousand troops from seven prefectures with authority to mobilize them, orders to deliver grain levies from Southern Qin and Eastern Yi to the garrisons, freedom to draft commanders from western governors, and full control of military supplies and seals.

sentences.zh: 普惠至南秦，停岐、涇、華、雍、豳、東秦六州兵武，召秦州兵武四千人，分配四統；

translations.literal: Puhui reached Southern Qin, halted the troops of Qi, Jing, Hua, Yong, Bin, and Eastern Qin — six prefectures — summoned four thousand troops of Qin prefecture, and assigned them to four commands;
translations.idiomatic: At Southern Qin, Puhui stood down troops from six prefectures, summoned four thousand from Qin prefecture, and divided them into four commands;

sentences.zh: 令送租兵連營接柵，相繼而進，運租車驢，隨機輸轉。

translations.literal: he ordered grain-escort troops in linked camps and connected palisades to advance in succession; carts and donkeys transporting grain rotated supply as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Grain convoys marched in linked camps and palisades while carts and pack animals rotated supplies as needed.

sentences.zh: 別遣中散大夫封答慰喻南秦，員外常侍楊公熙宣勞東益氐民。

translations.literal: Separately he dispatched Palace Attendant Feng Da to comfort and instruct Southern Qin, and Extraordinary Palace Attendant Yang Gongxi to proclaim rewards and soothe the Di people of Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent palace attendant Feng Da to reassure Southern Qin and extraordinary attendant Yang Gongxi to mollify the Di of Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 於時，南秦氐豪吳富聚合兇類，所在邀劫。

translations.literal: At that time, Southern Qin Di magnate Wu Fu gathered violent factions and waylaid and robbed wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wu Fu, a Di magnate of Southern Qin, gathered outlaws and preyed on travelers everywhere.

sentences.zh: 公熙既至東益州，刺史魏子建密與普惠書，言公熙舊是蕃國之胤，而諸氐與相見者，必有陰私言，宜加圖防。

translations.literal: Once Gongxi reached Eastern Yi, Inspector Wei Zijian secretly wrote Puhui saying Gongxi was formerly of barbarian-state lineage, and when the various Di met and saw him there must be private talk — precautions ought to be increased.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongxi reached Eastern Yi, inspector Wei Zijian secretly warned Puhui that as a descendant of a frontier kingdom, Gongxi would hold private talks with the Di and should be watched closely.

sentences.zh: 普惠乃符攝公熙，令赴南秦。

translations.literal: Puhui then issued a warrant summoning Gongxi, ordering him to proceed to Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui issued a summons ordering Gongxi to report to Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 公熙果已密遣其從兄山虎與吳富同逆，又妄自說鄉里，紛動羣氐，託云與崔南秦有隙，拒而不赴。

translations.literal: Gongxi indeed had secretly sent his older cousin Shanhu to rebel together with Wu Fu; he also falsely spoke on his own of his home region, stirring up the Di tribes, claiming a feud with Cui of Southern Qin, and refused to come.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxi had already secretly sent his cousin Shanhu to rebel with Wu Fu; he agitated the Di with false tales of hometown grievances, claimed a feud with Cui of Southern Qin, and refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 租達平落，吳富等果脅車營，實公熙所潛遣也。

translations.literal: When grain reached Pingluo, Wu Fu and the rest indeed forced and robbed the cart camps — in truth it was what Gongxi had secretly dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: When grain reached Pingluo, Wu Fu raided the convoys — exactly as Gongxi had secretly arranged.

sentences.zh: 後吳富雖為左右所殺，而徒黨猶盛。

translations.literal: Later, though Wu Fu was killed by his own followers, the party remained strong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fu was later killed by his own men, but the band remained powerful.

sentences.zh: 秦□所綰武都、武階，租頗得達。

translations.literal: In the Qin [□] sector he held Wudu and Wujie, and grain largely managed to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qin prefecture area he held Wudu and Wujie, and much of the grain got through.

sentences.zh: 東益羣氐先款順，故廣業、仇鳩、河池三城粟便得入。

translations.literal: The Di tribes of Eastern Yi had first submitted peacefully, so grain at Guangye, Qiuchou, and Hechi — three cities — promptly entered.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Di of Eastern Yi had submitted first, grain reached Guangye, Qiuchou, and Hechi without trouble.

sentences.zh: 其應入東益十萬石租，皆稽留費盡，升斗不至，鎮戍兵武，遂致飢虛，咸恨普惠經略不廣。

translations.literal: The hundred thousand shi of grain rent that ought to have entered Eastern Yi — all were detained and spent; not a sheng or dou arrived; garrison troops and soldiers thus fell into hunger and want; all resented that Puhui's strategy was not broad enough.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred thousand shi owed Eastern Yi was consumed in delays — not a grain reached the garrisons, troops went hungry, and all blamed Puhui's narrow strategy.

sentences.zh: 事訖，普惠拜表按劾公熙。

translations.literal: When matters concluded, Puhui submitted a memorial to investigate and impeach Gongxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended, Puhui memorialized to impeach Gongxi.

sentences.zh: 還朝，賜絹布一百段。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was granted a hundred bolts of silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was rewarded with a hundred bolts of silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 時詔訪冤屈，普惠上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time an edict sought out cases of wrong and oppression; Puhui submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When an edict solicited cases of injustice, Puhui submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 詩稱「文王孫子，本枝百世」，易曰「大君有命，開國承家」。

translations.literal: The Odes says "King Wen's descendants, root and branch for a hundred generations"; the Changes says "The great lord has a command: establish states, inherit houses."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes praise "King Wen's descendants — root and branch for a hundred generations"; the Changes declare "The great lord commands: establish states and inherit houses."

sentences.zh: 皆所以明德睦親，維城作翰。

translations.literal: All are for making virtue bright, drawing kin close, erecting ramparts as balustrades.
translations.idiomatic: Both serve to display virtue, bind kin close, and make the royal house a fortress.

sentences.zh: 漢祖封爵之誓曰：「使黃河如帶，太山如礪，國以永存，爰及苗裔。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han's oath at enfeoffment said: "May the Yellow River become like a belt, Mount Tai like a whetstone — the state forever endures, reaching even to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's enfeoffment oath ran: "May the Yellow River become a ribbon and Mount Tai a grindstone — may the state endure forever, down to our descendants.

sentences.zh: 又申之以丹書之信，重之以白馬之盟。

translations.literal: He further affirmed it with red-scroll faith, and weighted it with the white-horse covenant.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed it with red-scroll edicts and the covenant of the white horse.

sentences.zh: 其以強大分王，罪犯蹙邑者，蓋有之矣，未聞父基子構，世載忠賢，一死一削，用為恒典者也。

translations.literal: That powerful men were divided into kings and crimes shriveled their fiefs — such cases have existed; but never have I heard of father laying foundation and son building on it, generation after generation bearing loyal worth, one death one reduction, used as a constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful lords have been enfeoffed and criminals stripped of fiefs — but never has a line built by father and son, generation after generation of loyal service, been cut on every death as fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 故尚書令臣肇，未能遠稽古義，近究成旨，以初封之詔，有親王二千戶、始蕃一千戶、二蕃五百戶、三蕃三百戶，謂是親疏世減之法；

translations.literal: Thus Minister of Works Ling, my lord, failed to examine ancient meaning from afar or investigate completed intent from near, and taking the initial enfeoffment edict — with imperial princes at two thousand households, first-rank vassal princes at one thousand, second-rank at five hundred, third-rank at three hundred — held this to be the law of diminishing by generation according to closeness of kin;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Ling failed to consult antiquity or the original intent, and read the initial enfeoffment quotas — two thousand households for imperial princes, one thousand for first-rank vassal princes, five hundred for second-rank, three hundred for third-rank — as a law of diminishing fiefs by generation according to kinship distance.

sentences.zh: 又以開國五等，有所減之言，以為世減之趣。

translations.literal: And further, from the statement that establishing states in five ranks involved reduction, he took this as the tendency of diminishing by generation.
translations.idiomatic: And from the phrase about reduction among the five ranks of enfeoffment he inferred a policy of hereditary reduction.

sentences.zh: 遂立格奏奪，稱是高祖本意，仍被旨可。

translations.literal: Thereupon regulations were established, memorials submitted, and confiscations carried out, claiming this was Emperor Gaozu's original intent; and the edict was approved.
translations.idiomatic: They then codified the rules, memorialized confiscations, and claimed this reflected Emperor Gaozu's original intent — and the edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 差謬之來，亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: The arrival of error and discrepancy has already gone too far.
translations.idiomatic: The errors had already become egregious.

sentences.zh: 遂使勳親懷屈，幽顯同冤，紛訟彌年，莫之能息。

translations.literal: Thus meritorious kin harbored grievance, the hidden and manifest alike shared injustice, lawsuits multiplied year on year, and none could quell them.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious kin were left aggrieved, the living and dead alike wronged; lawsuits dragged on for years with no end in sight.

sentences.zh: 臣輒遠研旨格，深窮其事，世變減奪，今古無據。

translations.literal: Your servant then examined edict provisions from afar and thoroughly investigated the matter; reduction and confiscation by generation has no precedent in antiquity or today.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined the edict provisions at length and investigated the matter thoroughly: hereditary reduction and confiscation has no warrant in past or present.

sentences.zh: 又尋詔書，稱昔未可采，今始列辭，豈得混一，罔分久近也。

translations.literal: Moreover, searching the edicts, it says what was past could not be adopted, and only now are arguments set forth — [11] how can one lump them together and disregard distinctions of old and recent.
translations.idiomatic: The edicts also state that earlier cases were not to be cited and only now should arguments be recorded — [11] how can old and recent cases be treated alike without regard to when they arose.

sentences.zh: 故樂良、樂安，同蕃異封；

translations.literal: [12] Thus Yue Liang and Yue'an — same rank as vassal princes, different enfeoffments;
translations.idiomatic: [12] Yue Liang and Yue'an held the same vassal-prince rank but received different fiefs;

sentences.zh: 廣陽、安豐，屬別戶等。

translations.literal: Guangyang and Anfeng — dependent separate households, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang and Anfeng were dependent on separate household registers, and so on.

sentences.zh: 安定之嫡，邑齊親王；

translations.literal: The legitimate heir of Anding — fief equal to an imperial prince;
translations.idiomatic: Anding's legitimate heir received a fief equal to an imperial prince;

sentences.zh: 河間戚近，更從蕃食。

translations.literal: Hejian, kin closely related, further received sustenance as a vassal prince.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian, a close imperial kinsman, additionally drew sustenance as a vassal prince.

sentences.zh: 是乃太和降旨，初封之倫級，勳親兼樹，非世減之大驗者也。

translations.literal: These were decrees issued in the Taihe era, the hierarchy of initial enfeoffment, merit and kin both established — not great proofs of hereditary reduction.
translations.idiomatic: These reflect Taihe-era decrees on the hierarchy of initial enfeoffment, enfeoffing both meritorious ministers and kin — not evidence of a policy of hereditary reduction.

sentences.zh: 博陵襲爵，亦在太和之年，時不世減，以父嘗全食，足戶充本，同之始封，減從今式。

translations.literal: Boling's inheriting the title also fell in the Taihe year — at the time there was no hereditary reduction; because the father once received full sustenance, sufficient households filled the original quota, equal to the initial enfeoffment, reduction followed the present formula.
translations.idiomatic: Boling's succession also occurred in the Taihe era, when hereditary reduction did not apply: because his father had once enjoyed full sustenance with households sufficient to fill the original quota, matching the initial enfeoffment, reduction followed today's formula.

sentences.zh: 如此，則減者減其所足之外，足者足其所減之內。

translations.literal: Thus, what was reduced was reduced beyond what sufficed; what sufficed filled within what was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Under this scheme, reduction applied only beyond what was sufficient, and sufficiency was maintained within what was reduced.

sentences.zh: 減足之旨，乃為所貢所食耳。

translations.literal: The intent of reduction-and-sufficiency was simply for what was contributed and what was consumed.
translations.idiomatic: The policy of reduction-and-sufficiency concerned only tribute owed and sustenance consumed.

sentences.zh: 欲使諸王開國，弗專其民，賦役之差，貴賤有等。

translations.literal: The aim was to keep princes who established states from monopolizing their people, and to differentiate tax and corvée by rank, noble and base having grades.
translations.idiomatic: The goal was to prevent enfeoffed princes from monopolizing their subjects and to maintain graded distinctions in taxes and corvée according to rank.

sentences.zh: 蓋準擬周禮公侯伯子男貢稅之法，王食其半，公食三分之一，侯、伯四分之一，子、男五分之一。

translations.literal: It modeled the Zhou Rites method of tribute and tax for duke, marquis, earl, viscount, and baron: the king consumed half, the duke a third, marquis and earl a quarter, viscount and baron a fifth.
translations.idiomatic: It followed the Zhou Rites scheme of graded tribute: the king took half, dukes a third, marquises and earls a quarter, viscounts and barons a fifth.

sentences.zh: 是以新興得足充本，清淵吏多減戶。

translations.literal: Thus Xinxing obtained sufficiency to fill its original quota, while Qingyuan's officials had many reduced households.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Xinxing received enough to fill its original quota, while Qingyuan saw many households reduced.

sentences.zh: 故始封承襲俱稱。

translations.literal: Therefore initial enfeoffment and hereditary succession were both so termed.
translations.idiomatic: Both initial enfeoffment and hereditary succession were governed by the same terminology.

sentences.zh: 所減謂減之以貢，食謂食之於國，斯實高祖霈然之詔。

translations.literal: "What was reduced" meant reduction in tribute; "sustenance" meant consuming from the state — this was truly Emperor Gaozu's magnanimous edict.
translations.idiomatic: "Reduction" meant cutting tribute payments; "sustenance" meant consuming revenues from the state — this was Emperor Gaozu's generous decree.

sentences.zh: 減實之理，聖明自釋，求之史帛，猶有未盡。

translations.literal: The principle of actual reduction the sage has himself explained; searching the historical records, some points remain incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of reduction has been explained by the sage emperor himself, yet searching the historical records, some points remain unclear.

sentences.zh: 時尚書臣琇疑減足之參差，旨又判之，以開訓所減之旨，可以不疑於世減矣。

translations.literal: At the time Minister Xiu questioned the discrepancies in reduction-and-sufficiency; the edict judged again, clarifying the intent of reduction — hereditary reduction need no longer be doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xiu once questioned discrepancies in the reduction-and-sufficiency policy; another imperial judgment clarified the intent of reduction, which should have settled any doubt about hereditary reduction.

sentences.zh: 而臣肇弗稽往事，曰五等有所減之格，用為世減之法；

translations.literal: Yet my lord Ling failed to verify past affairs, saying the five ranks had regulations involving reduction, using them as the law of hereditary reduction;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Minister of Works Ling failed to verify past precedents, holding that the five ranks' regulations on reduction constituted a law of hereditary reduction;

sentences.zh: 以王封有親疏之等，謂是代削之條。

translations.literal: and because prince enfeoffments had grades of closeness and distance, held this to be the article of reduction by generation.
translations.idiomatic: and because princely enfeoffments had grades of kinship distance, treated this as a rule of reduction by generation.

sentences.zh: 妄解成旨，雷同世奪。

translations.literal: He rashly misinterpreted the completed edict and uniformly followed hereditary confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: He misread the established edicts and applied hereditary confiscation across the board.

sentences.zh: 以此毒天下，民其從乎！

translations.literal: With this poisoning the realm — would the people follow!
translations.idiomatic: To poison the realm thus — would the people comply!

sentences.zh: 故太傅、任城文宣王臣澄樞弼累朝，識洞今古，為尚書之日，殷勤執請，孜孜於重議。

translations.literal: Thus Grand Tutor, Prince Wenxuan of Rencheng, my lord Cheng — pillar of successive courts, understanding penetrating past and present — when he served as Minister of Works, earnestly insisted and diligently pursued re-deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yuan Cheng, Prince Wenxuan of Rencheng — a pillar of successive reigns with penetrating knowledge of past and present — when he headed the Ministry of Works, earnestly petitioned and persistently sought redeliberation.

sentences.zh: 被旨不許，於此遂停。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it; at this it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused; and the matter stopped there.

sentences.zh: 又律罪例減，及先帝之緦麻；

translations.literal: Moreover, the code's provisions on mitigating punishment extended to the late emperor's distant kin in fine-hemp mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the code's provisions on mitigating punishment extended to the late emperor's distant kin in fine-hemp mourning;

sentences.zh: 令給親恤，止當世之有服。

translations.literal: the ordinance granting kin condolence allowances applied only to those in mourning in the present generation.
translations.idiomatic: while the ordinance granting kin condolence allowances applied only to those in mourning in the present generation.

sentences.zh: 律、令相違，威澤異品。

translations.literal: Code and ordinance conflicted; authority and favor differed in kind.
translations.idiomatic: The code and ordinance contradicted each other, and imperial favor fell unevenly.

sentences.zh: 使七廟曾玄，不治未恤，嫡封則爵祿無窮，枝庶則屬內貶絕。

translations.literal: This left great-great-grandsons of the seven temples without condolence allowances; legitimate heirs with enfeoffments enjoyed endless salary and rank, while collateral lines were degraded and cut off within the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Great-great-grandsons of the ancestral temple received no condolence allowances; legitimate heirs enjoyed endless rank and salary, while collateral branches were degraded and cast out.

sentences.zh: 儀刑作孚，億兆何觀。

translations.literal: Where the model of conduct inspires trust — what would the hundred million look to.
translations.idiomatic: When the model of conduct fails to inspire trust, what example do the masses have.

sentences.zh: 夫一人吁嗟，尚曰虧治。

translations.literal: When even one person sighs in lament, it is said governance suffers.
translations.idiomatic: Even a single person's lament is said to mar good governance.

sentences.zh: 今諸王五等，各稱其冤；

translations.literal: Now the princes of five ranks each claim their grievance;
translations.idiomatic: Now the princes of five ranks each proclaim their grievance;

sentences.zh: 七廟之孫，並訟其切。

translations.literal: descendants of the seven temples all plead their distress.
translations.idiomatic: and descendants of the ancestral temple all plead their distress.

sentences.zh: 陳訴之案，盈於省曹，朝言巷議，咸云其苦。

translations.literal: Cases of petition overflowed the ministries; court talk and alley gossip alike spoke of their suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions overflowed the ministries; at court and in the streets alike, all spoke of their plight.

sentences.zh: 恐非先王所以建萬國，親諸侯，睦九族之義也。

translations.literal: I fear this is not the meaning of the former kings in establishing myriad states, drawing close the feudal lords, and harmonizing the nine kin-groups.
translations.idiomatic: This scarcely accords with the ancient purpose of establishing myriad states, drawing feudal lords close, and harmonizing the nine kin-groups.

sentences.zh: 臣猥忝今任，於茲五年，推尋旨格，謂無世減之理。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly holds the present post; in these five years, searching edict provisions, I find no principle of hereditary reduction.
translations.idiomatic: In the five years I have humbly held this post, examining the edict provisions, I find no basis for hereditary reduction.

sentences.zh: 請近遵高祖減食之謨，遠循百代象賢之誥，退由九伐，進從九儀，則刑罰有倫，封不虛黜。

translations.literal: I ask that we follow Emperor Gaozu's plan on reducing sustenance in the near term, and in the long term follow the hundred generations' injunction to honor the worthy; demotions according to the Nine Punishments, promotions according to the Nine Etiquettes — then punishments and rewards would have order, and enfeoffments would not be vacated without cause.
translations.idiomatic: I urge adherence to Emperor Gaozu's plan for reducing sustenance and, looking to antiquity, the injunction to honor worthy successors; demotions by the Nine Punishments, promotions by the Nine Etiquettes — then punishments would be orderly and fiefs would not be stripped without cause.

sentences.zh: 斯乃文王所以克慎，不敢侮於鰥寡，而況於公侯伯子男乎？

translations.literal: This is how King Wen was able to be cautious — not daring to wrong widowers and widows — how much more for duke, marquis, earl, viscount, and baron?
translations.idiomatic: This is the caution of King Wen, who did not wrong widowers and widows — how much more should we not wrong dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons?

sentences.zh: 今旨訪冤滯，愚以此為大者。

translations.literal: Now the edict inquires into grievances left unresolved; your servant considers this the greatest matter.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the throne seeks unresolved grievances, I consider this the greatest issue.

sentences.zh: 求尋光錫之詔，并諸條格，所奪所請，事事窮審。

translations.literal: I ask to trace edicts of glorious bestowal and all regulations — what was confiscated and what was requested — examining each item thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: I urge a thorough review of edicts of glorious bestowal and all regulations — every confiscation and every petition investigated to the end.

sentences.zh: 諸王開國，非犯罪削奪者，並求還復。

translations.literal: For princes who established states, those not stripped for crimes — I ask that all be restored.
translations.idiomatic: For enfeoffed princes stripped without criminal cause, I ask full restoration.

sentences.zh: 其昔嘗全食，足戶充本，減從令式者，從前則力多於親懿，全奪則減足之格不行，愚謂祿力並應依所□之食而食之。

translations.literal: Those who once received full sustenance, with households sufficient to fill the original quota, reduction following present formula — looking back, salary quota exceeded kin of close relation; total confiscation would leave the reduction-and-sufficiency provision unworkable; your servant holds salary and quota should both follow the sustenance □ allotted and consume thereby.
translations.idiomatic: For those who once enjoyed full sustenance with households filling the original quota, with reduction following present formula — in the past their salary quota exceeded that of close imperial kin; total confiscation would nullify the reduction-and-sufficiency rule. I hold that salary and quota should both follow the allotted sustenance □ and be consumed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 若是則力少蕃王，粟帛仍本戶邑雖盈之減。

translations.literal: If so, then salary quota would be less than vassal princes', yet grain and silk would still derive from the original fief households — though full, subject to reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Thus princes would receive smaller salary quotas than other vassal kings, while grain and silk would still come from their original household fiefs — subject to reduction even when ample.

sentences.zh: 兩秦既有全食足戶之異，[13]故不得同於新封之力耳。

translations.literal: The two Qin princes already differ in full sustenance and sufficient households — [13] therefore they cannot be treated the same as newly enfeoffed salary quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The two Qin princes already differ in full sustenance and sufficient households — [13] they cannot be equated with the salary quotas of newly enfeoffed princes.

sentences.zh: 親恤所裒，請依律斷。

translations.literal: As for kin condolence allowances that were withheld, I ask that judgment follow the code.
translations.idiomatic: For withheld kin condolence allowances, I ask judgment according to the code.

sentences.zh: 伏惟親親尊賢，位必功立。

translations.literal: Humbly considering — drawing kin close and honoring the worthy — position must be established through merit.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing kin close and honoring the worthy — rank must be earned through merit.

sentences.zh: 尊賢以司民，可不慎乎？

translations.literal: Honoring the worthy to govern the people — can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: To honor the worthy in governing the people — can one be anything but cautious?

sentences.zh: 親親以牧族，其可棄乎？

translations.literal: Drawing kin close to shepherd the clan — can one abandon this?
translations.idiomatic: To draw kin close in shepherding the clan — can one cast this aside?

sentences.zh: 如脫蒙允，求以旨判為始，其前來吏秩，悉年久不追。

translations.literal: If by chance my request is granted, I ask that the edict judgment serve as the starting point; prior official ranks and salaries — all past years not to be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: If this is granted, I ask that the imperial judgment mark a fresh start; prior salary and rank adjustments from years past should not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞明德慎罰，文王所以造周；

translations.literal: Your servant further hears that bright virtue and careful punishment — this is how King Wen created Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: I further recall that bright virtue and careful punishment — this is how King Wen founded Zhou;

sentences.zh: 咸有一德，殷湯所以革夏。

translations.literal: all sharing one virtue — this is how Tang of Yin overthrew Xia.
translations.idiomatic: sharing one virtue throughout — this is how King Tang overthrew the Xia.

sentences.zh: 故能上令下從，風動草偃，畏之如雷電，敬之如明神。

translations.literal: Thus they could have orders above and compliance below, wind moves grass bends; feared like thunder and lightning, revered like bright spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Thus commands from above met compliance below like wind bending grass; the people feared them as thunder and revered them as spirits.

sentences.zh: 是以天子家天下，綏萬國，若天之無不覆，地之無不載。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven makes the realm his household, pacifying myriad states — like heaven covering all, earth bearing all.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven treats the realm as his household and pacifies all states, like heaven covering all and earth bearing all.

sentences.zh: 遷都之構，庶方子來，汎澤所沾，降及陪皂。

translations.literal: At the capital transfer, common folk and lords came from afar; the general bounty reached even attendants and menials.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved, lords and commoners came from all directions; the general bounty reached even the lowliest attendants.

sentences.zh: 寧有岳牧、二千石、縣令、丞、尉、治中、別駕及諸軍幢，受命於朝廷，而可不預乎？

translations.literal: Can there be provincial governors, two-thousand-shi officials, county magistrates, assistants, wardens, clerks, provincial aides, and military commanders — all receiving appointments from the court — who would not participate?
translations.idiomatic: Surely provincial governors, two-thousand-shi officials, magistrates and their deputies, provincial aides, and military commanders — all commissioned by the court — were included?

sentences.zh: 此之班駁，雲雨之不平，謂是當時有司出納之未允。

translations.literal: This uneven distribution, this imbalance of cloud and rain — I hold it was because the officials of the time dispensed and collected unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: This patchwork of unequal treatment — this imbalance of rain — stemmed from officials' unjust disbursements.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this shown?
translations.idiomatic: How can this be demonstrated?

sentences.zh: 仰尋世宗詔書，百官普進一級，中有朝臣刺史登時褒授，則內外貴賤，莫不同澤。

translations.literal: Looking up to Emperor Xiaoming's edict — all officials promoted one rank universally; among them court ministers and inspectors were immediately commended and appointed — then inside and outside, noble and base, all shared the same bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong's edict promoted all officials one rank; court ministers and inspectors received immediate commendation — noble and humble, inside and outside, all shared the same bounty.

sentences.zh: 又覆奏稱爰及陪皂，明無不逮。

translations.literal: The follow-up memorial also stated that it extended even to attendants and menials — clearly none were left out.
translations.idiomatic: The follow-up memorial explicitly extended the bounty even to attendants and menials — clearly omitting none.

sentences.zh: 自後人率其心紛綸，盈庭嫌少，誤惑視聽。

translations.literal: Afterward people indulged their own inclinations in confusion; the court-full complained it was too little, misleading sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward officials followed their own inclinations in confusion; the court complained the bounty was too small, misleading judgment.

sentences.zh: 限以汎前，更為年斷。

translations.literal: Limited by pre-general-promotion status, converted to a cutoff by years.
translations.idiomatic: They imposed limits based on pre-promotion service and converted them to year-based cutoffs.

sentences.zh: 六年、三年之考，以意折之；

translations.literal: six-year and three-year performance reviews were arbitrarily discounted;
translations.idiomatic: Six-year and three-year performance reviews were arbitrarily discounted;

sentences.zh: 汎前、汎後之歲，隔而絕之。

translations.literal: years before and after general promotion were separated and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: years before and after the general promotion were separated and cut off.

sentences.zh: 遂使如綸之旨，頓於一朝。

translations.literal: Thus edicts as fine as silk thread collapsed in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus edicts as authoritative as imperial commands collapsed overnight.

sentences.zh: 汎前六年上第者全不得汎，三年上第者蒙半階而已。

translations.literal: Those with top ratings before general promotion for six years received no general promotion at all; those with top ratings for three years received only half a rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those with six years of top ratings before the general promotion received no promotion at all; those with three years received only half a rank.

sentences.zh: 汎前汎後合考者隔絕而不得，無考者無折而全。

translations.literal: Those whose combined reviews before and after general promotion ought to count were separated and denied; those without reviews were not discounted but received the full benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Combined pre- and post-promotion reviews were severed and denied; those without reviews faced no discount and received full promotion.

sentences.zh: 汎前汎後，有考無考，並蒙全汎。

translations.literal: Before and after general promotion, with or without reviews — all should receive the full general promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after the general promotion, with or without reviews — all should have received the full promotion.

sentences.zh: 與否乖違，勤舊彌屈。

translations.literal: Granting and denying at odds, the diligent and veteran were ever more aggrieved.
translations.idiomatic: Grants and denials contradicted each other; the diligent and long-serving grew ever more wronged.

sentences.zh: 差若毫釐，謬以千里，其此之謂乎？

translations.literal: Error like a hair's breadth, mistake of a thousand li — is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: A hairsbreadth of error leading to a thousand-li mistake — is this not the case?

sentences.zh: 易曰：「言行，君子之所以動天下，可不慎歟！」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Words and conduct — how the gentleman moves the realm — [15] can one not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Words and conduct — how the gentleman moves the realm — [15] can one not be cautious!"

sentences.zh: 言之不從，無以抑之，遂奏奪牧守外祿，全不與汎。

translations.literal: When words were not followed, there was nothing to restrain them; they then memorialized stripping governors' external salaries, giving no general promotion at all.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict went unheeded, nothing restrained them; they memorialized stripping provincial governors of external salaries and denied them general promotion entirely.

sentences.zh: 散官改為四年之考，汎前者八年一階。

translations.literal: Unattached offices were changed to four-year reviews; those before general promotion — one rank every eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Unattached offices were given four-year reviews; pre-promotion officials advanced one rank every eight years.

sentences.zh: 政令不一，冤訟惟甚，與而復奪，其本在茲。

translations.literal: Government orders were inconsistent; grievances were extreme; granted then confiscated again — the root lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Policies were inconsistent; grievances multiplied; benefits granted then withdrawn — the root cause lies here.

sentences.zh: 致使邀駕擊鼓者，無理以加其罪；

translations.literal: This caused those who waylaid the imperial carriage and struck the drum — there was no basis to punish their crime;
translations.idiomatic: Those who blocked the imperial procession to beat the grievance drum could not be punished;

sentences.zh: 誹謗公聽者，無辭以抑其言。

translations.literal: those who slandered before public hearings — no argument to suppress their words.
translations.idiomatic: and those who criticized openly could not be silenced.

sentences.zh: 噂𠴲所由生，慢勃所由起。

translations.literal: Slander thereby arises; insolence and rebellion thereby begin.
translations.idiomatic: From this slander arises; from this insolence and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 夫琴瑟不調，澆而更張。

translations.literal: When lute and zither are out of tune — discard and restring.
translations.idiomatic: When the lute and zither are out of tune, restring them.

sentences.zh: 善人，國之本也，其可棄乎？

translations.literal: Good men are the root of the state — can one abandon them?
translations.idiomatic: Good men are the foundation of the state — can they be cast aside?

sentences.zh: 詩云：「樂只君子，邦家之基。」

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Happy is the noble lord — foundation of state and family."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "Happy is the noble lord — foundation of state and family."

sentences.zh: 堯典曰：「克明俊德。」

translations.literal: The Canon of Yao says: "He was able to illumine lofty virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Yao says: "He was able to illumine lofty virtue."

sentences.zh: 呂刑曰：「何擇非人。」

translations.literal: The Punishments of Lü says: "How choose unworthy men."
translations.idiomatic: The Punishments of Lü says: "How choose unworthy men."

sentences.zh: 周官曰：「官弗必備惟其人。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou says: "Offices need not all be filled — only the right men."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou says: "Offices need not all be filled — only the right men."

sentences.zh: 咎繇曰：「無曠庶官，天工人其代之。」

translations.literal: Gao Yao said: "Let no office be vacant — Heaven's work, men must fulfill it."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yao said: "Let no office be vacant — Heaven's work, men must fulfill it."

sentences.zh: 詩云：「人之云亡，邦國殄悴。」

translations.literal: The Odes says: "When good men depart, state and realm wither."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "When good men depart, state and realm wither."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Rain on our lord's field reaches our private plots too."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Rain on our lord's field reaches our private plots too."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「不患貧而患不均。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Do not worry about poverty but worry about inequality."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Do not worry about poverty but worry about inequality."

sentences.zh: [17]如此，則官必擇人，汎則宜溥。

translations.literal: [17] Thus — offices must select the right men; general promotion should be broad.
translations.idiomatic: [17] From this it follows that offices must select the right men, and general promotion should be broad.

sentences.zh: 請遠遵正始元旨，近準聖明二汎，內外百官，悉同一階，不以汎前折考，不以散任增年，則同雲共澍，四海均洽。

translations.literal: I ask to follow far the original intent of Zhengshi, follow near the sage emperor's two general promotions — all officials inside and outside, uniformly one rank; not discounting reviews by pre-promotion status, not adding years for unattached appointments — then common clouds and shared rain, the four seas equally harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: I urge adherence to the original Zhengshi policy and the two sage general promotions: all officials within and without advanced one rank uniformly, without discounting reviews for pre-promotion service or extending years for unattached posts — then bounty would fall like rain across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 如謂未可，宜以權理折之。

translations.literal: If this is held not feasible, it should be resolved by expedient principle.
translations.idiomatic: If this cannot be adopted outright, a reasonable compromise should be found.

sentences.zh: 易曰：「聖人之大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The sage's great treasure is position — how does one guard position? By benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "The sage's great treasure is position — how does one guard position? By benevolence."

sentences.zh: 春秋傳曰：「一曰擇人。」

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: "First: select men."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: "First: select men."

sentences.zh: 如此，則乃可無汎，不可無考。

translations.literal: Thus — general promotion may be omitted, but performance review cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that general promotion may be omitted, but performance review cannot.

sentences.zh: 守宰之汎，既以追奪，則百官之汎，不應獨霑。

translations.literal: Provincial governors' general promotion having been retroactively confiscated, other officials' general promotion should not alone be favored.
translations.idiomatic: If provincial governors' promotions were retroactively revoked, other officials should not alone keep theirs.

sentences.zh: 溥澤既收，復誰敢怨！

translations.literal: Once broad bounty is withdrawn — who would dare complain!
translations.idiomatic: Once the broad bounty is withdrawn, who would dare complain!

sentences.zh: 夫三載之考，興於太和；

translations.literal: The three-year performance review arose in the Taihe era;
translations.idiomatic: The three-year performance review originated in the Taihe era;

sentences.zh: 再周之陟，通於景明。

translations.literal: promotion every two cycles was established in the Jingming era.
translations.idiomatic: promotion every two cycles was established in the Jingming era.

sentences.zh: 閑劇祿力，自有加減。

translations.literal: For lighter and heavier duties, salary quota had its own additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: Salary quotas for lighter and heavier posts naturally varied.

sentences.zh: 陪臣以事省降，而考則三年；

translations.literal: Attendant officials were reduced for lighter duties, yet their review remained three years;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant officials were reduced for lighter duties, yet their review remained three years;

sentences.zh: 朝官既祿等平曹，更四周乃陟。

translations.literal: Court officials — their salary grades equal to peers in the bureau — required four more cycles before promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials, whose salaries matched their bureau peers, required four full cycles before advancement.

sentences.zh: 考祿參差，各稱其枉。

translations.literal: Review and salary were uneven; each claimed injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Performance reviews and salaries were uneven, and each man claimed he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 且一日從軍征戍，苦於煩任終年；

translations.literal: Moreover, a single day following the army on campaign was as taxing as a full year's onerous duties;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a single day on campaign with the army was as exhausting as a full year of onerous office work;

sentences.zh: 專使決斷，重於陪臣恒上。

translations.literal: Exclusive envoys with decision-making power weighed more than attendant officials regularly serving at court.
translations.idiomatic: special envoys with decision-making authority counted for more than attendant officials who served regularly at court.

sentences.zh: 若通為三載之考，無汎隔折，則各盈其分，亦足以近塞羣口，遠綏四方。

translations.literal: If all were placed under a unified three-year review, without broad exemptions or reductions, then each would receive his full portion — enough to quiet critics nearby and reassure the realm from afar.
translations.idiomatic: If everyone were subject to a uniform three-year review, without broad exemptions or deductions, each would receive his full due — enough to silence critics at court and reassure the realm from afar.

sentences.zh: 日昳求賢，猶有所失，況不遵擇人之訓，唯以停久而進乎？

translations.literal: Even when seeking the worthy from morning to evening one still misses some — how much less when one ignores the teaching to select men and promotes solely on the basis of tenure?
translations.idiomatic: Even when seeking the worthy from dawn to dusk one still misses some — how much less when one ignores the teaching to select men and promotes solely on the basis of long service?

sentences.zh: 自今已後，考黜願以三宅革心，選進願以三儁居德。

translations.literal: From this day forward, for review and dismissal I ask that the Three Dwellings reform the heart be followed; for selection and promotion I ask that the Three Excellences match virtue to office be followed.
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, I ask that dismissals after review follow the Three Dwellings principle of reforming the heart, and that selections and promotions follow the Three Excellences principle of matching virtue to office.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「舉能其官，惟爾之能，稱非其人，惟爾弗任。」

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Raise men who can fulfill their office — that shows your ability; praise men unfit for their post — that shows you refuse the task."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "Raise men who can fulfill their office — that shows your ability; praise men unfit for their post — that shows you refuse the task."

sentences.zh: 斯周道所以佑辟康民，敢不敬守。

translations.literal: This is how the Zhou way supported the sovereign and brought peace to the people; how could I fail to respect and keep it?
translations.idiomatic: This is how the Zhou way supported the sovereign and brought peace to the people — how could I fail to respect and uphold it?

sentences.zh: 臣忝官樞副，毗察冤訟，寤寐惟省，謂宜追正，愚固所陳，萬無可採。

translations.literal: Your subject holds a deputy post at the chief secretariat, assisting in examining wrongful lawsuits; waking and sleeping I reflect on this and believe it ought to be corrected. What this fool has put forward has not a single point worth taking up.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a deputy post at the chief secretariat, assisting in the examination of wrongful lawsuits; waking and sleeping I reflect on this and believe the system ought to be corrected. What this fool has put forward has not a single point worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 出除左將軍、東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed outside the capital as Left General and Governor of Eastern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed outside the capital as Left General and Governor of Eastern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南九戍、十三郡，猶因蕭衍前弊，別郡異縣之民錯雜居止。

translations.literal: The nine garrisons and thirteen commanderies of Huainan still bore the disarray left by Xiao Yan's earlier rule, with people from different commanderies and counties living intermingled.
translations.idiomatic: The nine garrisons and thirteen commanderies of Huainan still suffered from the disorder left by Xiao Yan's earlier rule, with people from different commanderies and counties living intermingled.

sentences.zh: 普惠乃依次括比，省減郡縣，上表陳狀。

translations.literal: Puhui then conducted a sequential census and comparison, reduced counties and commanderies, and submitted a memorial describing the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui then conducted a sequential census and comparison, reduced the number of counties and commanderies, and submitted a memorial describing the situation.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 宰守因此綰攝有方，姦盜不起，民以為便。

translations.literal: As a result the governors and prefects gained effective control, banditry and theft ceased, and the people found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the governors and prefects gained effective control, banditry and theft ceased, and the people found the arrangement convenient.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將胡廣來寇安陽，軍主陳明祖等脅白沙、鹿城二戍，衍又遣定州刺史田超秀、田僧達等竊陷石頭戍，徑據安陂城。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent General Hu Guang to attack Anyang; Garrison Commander Chen Mingzu and others pressured the garrisons at Baisha and Lucheng; Yan also sent the Governor of Dingzhou Tian Chaoqiu, Tian Sengda, and others to seize Shitou Garrison by stealth and occupy Anpi City directly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent General Hu Guang to attack Anyang; Garrison Commander Chen Mingzu and others pressured the garrisons at Baisha and Lucheng; Yan also sent the Governor of Dingzhou Tian Chaoqiu, Tian Sengda, and others to seize Shitou Garrison by stealth and occupy Anpi City directly.

sentences.zh: 郢州新塘之賊，近在州西數十里。

translations.literal: The bandits at Xintang in Ying Province were just a few dozen li west of the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits at Xintang in Ying Province were just a few dozen li west of the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 普惠前後命將拒戰，並破之。

translations.literal: Puhui repeatedly sent generals to resist the attacks and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui repeatedly sent generals to resist the attacks and defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 普惠不營財業，好有進舉，敦於故舊。

translations.literal: Puhui did not pursue personal wealth, took pleasure in advancing worthy men, and was devoted to old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui did not pursue personal wealth, took pleasure in advancing worthy men, and was devoted to old friends.

sentences.zh: 冀州人侯堅固少時與其遊學，早終，其子長瑜，普惠每於四時請祿，無不減贍給其衣食。

translations.literal: A man of Jizhou named Hou Jiangu had studied with him in youth and died young; his son Changyu — every season when Puhui requested his salary he always set aside a portion to provide the boy food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Jizhou named Hou Jiangu had studied with him in youth and died young; his son Changyu — every season when Puhui requested his salary he always set aside a portion to provide the boy with food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 及為豫州，啟長瑜解褐，攜其合門拯給之。

translations.literal: When he became Governor of Yuzhou, he recommended Changyu for initial appointment and supported his entire household.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Governor of Yuzhou, he recommended Changyu for initial appointment and supported his entire household.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年三月，在州卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Xiaochang he died in office, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Xiaochang he died in office, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈平北將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰宣恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous name Xuangong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous name Xuangong.

sentences.zh: 長子榮儁，武定末，齊王相府屬。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rongjun, at the end of the Wuding era, was an aide in the Prince of Qi's chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Rongjun, at the end of the Wuding era, was an aide in the Prince of Qi's chancellery.

sentences.zh: 榮儁弟龍子，揚州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: Rongjun's younger brother Longzi was chief administrator of the Yangzhou General of Agile Cavalry's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Rongjun's younger brother Longzi was chief administrator on the staff of the Yangzhou General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孫紹關右之士，[18]又能指論世務，亦其志也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Sun Shao was a man of Guanzhong, [18] and could also discuss affairs of the age — that was his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Sun Shao was a man of Guanzhong, [18] and could also discuss affairs of the age — that was his ambition.

sentences.zh: 張普惠明達典故，強直從官，侃然不撓，其有王臣之風矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Puhui had clear mastery of precedent and ritual, was upright as a court official, and spoke boldly without yielding — he had the bearing of a true minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Puhui had clear mastery of precedent and ritual, was upright as a court official, and spoke boldly without yielding — he had the bearing of a true minister.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 臣卿乃少 諸本「卿」作「節」，北史卷四六孫紹傳、冊府卷九四六

translations.literal: On "Your subject, the Director, is young": in various editions "Director" (qing) is written as "Controller" (jie); the biography of Sun Shao in juan 46 of the History of the Northern Dynasties and juan 946 of the Cefu Yuangui
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Your subject, the Director, is young": various editions read "Director" (qing) as "Controller" (jie); the biography of Sun Shao in juan 46 of the History of the Northern Dynasties and juan 946 of the Cefu Yuangui

sentences.zh: 〈一一一四二頁〉
作「卿」。

translations.literal: read "Director."
translations.idiomatic: read "Director."

sentences.zh: 按孫紹這時官太府少卿，故作此語，「節」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Sun Shao at this time held the post of Vice Director of the Grand Treasury, hence this wording; "Controller" is corrupt, and the text is now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao at this time held the post of Vice Director of the Grand Treasury, hence this wording; "Controller" is corrupt, and the text is corrected here accordingly.

sentences.zh: 葬我小君文姜氏 北史卷四六張普惠傳無「氏」字。

translations.literal: On "Bury my young lady Wen Jiang shi": the biography of Zhang Puhui in juan 46 of the History of the Northern Dynasties lacks the character "shi."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Bury my young lady Wen Jiang shi": the biography of Zhang Puhui in juan 46 of the History of the Northern Dynasties lacks the character "shi."

sentences.zh: 按春秋莊公二十二年經文本無「氏」字，這裏當是衍文。

translations.literal: The canonical text of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang, year 22, has no character "shi"; here it is probably a superfluous addition.
translations.idiomatic: The canonical text of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang, year 22, has no character "shi"; here it is probably a superfluous addition.

sentences.zh: 又曰不為君母之黨服則為其母之黨服 按禮記未見此語，唯服問云：「為其母之黨服，則不為繼母之黨服。」

translations.literal: It also says: "If one does not wear mourning for the mother's kin on the father's side, then one wears mourning for the mother's kin on the mother's side." This phrase is not found in the Book of Rites; only the Fu Wen says: "If one wears mourning for the mother's kin on the mother's side, then one does not wear mourning for the mother's kin on the stepmother's side."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "If one does not wear mourning for the mother's kin on the father's side, then one wears mourning for the mother's kin on the mother's side." This phrase is not found in the Book of Rites; only the Fu Wen says: "If one wears mourning for the mother's kin on the mother's side, then one does not wear mourning for the mother's kin on the stepmother's side."

sentences.zh: 疑普惠即用此文而倒其辭，則「君」字當是「繼」字之訛。

translations.literal: Puhui probably drew on this passage and reversed its wording; then the character "lord" (jun) should be the corrupt form of "step" (ji).
translations.idiomatic: Puhui probably drew on this passage and reversed its wording; the character "lord" (jun) should be the corrupt form of "step" (ji).

sentences.zh: 普惠諸奏疏中引經文與今傳本間有出入，或是誤記，或當時傳抄本有異文，不悉出校記。

translations.literal: In Puhui's various memorials, quotations from the classics sometimes differ from current transmitted texts — whether through misquotation or variant readings in copies of his day — not all such cases are noted in the collation.
translations.idiomatic: In Puhui's various memorials, quotations from the classics sometimes differ from current transmitted texts — whether through misquotation or variant readings in copies of his day — and not all such cases are noted in the collation.

sentences.zh: 禮有下卿上士 冊府卷五四一

translations.literal: On "In ritual there are lower grand masters and upper servicemen": Cefu Yuangui juan 541
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "In ritual there are lower grandees and upper servicemen": Cefu Yuangui juan 541

translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 6494〉

translations.literal: reads "lower grand master" as "upper grand master."
translations.idiomatic: reads "lower grand master" as "upper grand master."

sentences.zh: 按這是張普惠駁袁翻「上公」「上大夫」的話，所重在「上」字，諸本作「下卿」當訛。

translations.literal: This is Zhang Puhui's rebuttal of Yuan Fan's "upper duke" and "upper grand master"; the emphasis is on the character "upper"; various editions reading "lower grand master" are probably corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: This is Zhang Puhui's rebuttal of Yuan Fan's "upper duke" and "upper grand master"; the emphasis is on the character "upper"; various editions reading "lower grand master" are probably corrupt.

sentences.zh: 時中山莊弼遺書普惠曰 北史卷四六「莊」作「杜」。

translations.literal: On "At that time Zhuang Bi of Zhongshan sent a letter to Puhui saying": in juan 46 of the History of the Northern Dynasties "Zhuang" is written as "Du."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "At that time Zhuang Bi of Zhongshan sent a letter to Puhui saying": in juan 46 of the History of the Northern Dynasties "Zhuang" is written as "Du."

sentences.zh: 按北齊書卷二四杜弼傳云：「中山曲陽人也。」

translations.literal: The biography of Du Bi in juan 24 of the History of the Northern Qi says: "A native of Quyang in Zhongshan."
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Du Bi in juan 24 of the History of the Northern Qi says: "A native of Quyang in Zhongshan."

sentences.zh: 當即其人。

translations.literal: He must be the same man.
translations.idiomatic: He must be the same man.

sentences.zh: 這裏「莊」字當是形近而訛。

translations.literal: Here the character "Zhuang" is probably a corruption through graphic similarity.
translations.idiomatic: Here the character "Zhuang" is probably a corruption through graphic similarity.

sentences.zh: 不適於綿麻而已 通鑑卷一四八

translations.literal: On "It does not extend beyond hempen mourning alone": Zizhi Tongjian juan 148
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "It does not extend beyond hempen mourning alone": Zizhi Tongjian juan 148

translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 4636〉

translations.idiomatic: reads "extend to" (shi) as "merely" (chi); this is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 不惟法度之□易 冊府卷五三０

translations.literal: On "It is not only that legal standards are □ easy": Cefu Yuangui juan 530
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "It is not only that legal standards are □ easy": Cefu Yuangui juan 530

translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 6336〉

translations.literal: The missing character is given as "width" (fu), which makes no sense; it is not supplied here.
translations.idiomatic: The missing character is given as "width" (fu), which makes no sense; it is not supplied here.

sentences.zh: 今宮人請調度 按上云「羣官共竊之」，下云「百官請俸」，疑「宮人」乃「官人」之訛。

translations.literal: On "Now palace women request allotments": above it says "the officials all steal them together," below it says "the hundred officials request salaries" — "palace women" (gong ren) is probably the corrupt form of "officials" (guan ren).
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Now palace women request allotments": above it says "the officials all steal them together," below it says "the hundred officials request salaries" — "palace women" (gong ren) is probably the corrupt form of "officials" (guan ren).

sentences.zh: 總常俸之數千俸所出以布綿麻亦應其一歲之用 按語意晦澀，疑有訛脫。

translations.literal: On "The total of regular salaries — the thousands of salaries disbursed in cloth, cotton, and hemp should also meet one year's needs": the sense is obscure; there is probably corruption or omission.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "The total of regular salaries — the thousands of salaries disbursed in cloth, cotton, and hemp should also meet one year's needs": the sense is obscure; there is probably corruption or omission.

translations.idiomatic: Regarding "This fool suggests following the precedent of morning and evening": Zizhi Tongjian juan 148
